Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side — see presentation_router.json → dual_group_rules['9811-9819'].

morphology_entries.morphology_name: B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with t(1;19)(q23;p13.3); E2A-PBX1 (TCF3-PBX1)
morphology_entries.coding_note: t(1;19) TCF3::PBX1. Phenotypic prompt only, never a code substitute: CD9 strong with CD34 negative (§3.2, Group 1 §3.1). Reached from the Group II side only when the disease is a nodal or extranodal lymphoblastic lymphoma; a marrow-primary case is Group I (see topography_routing_note). diagnostic_tests_required names Cytogenetics/FISH because FISH is the modality Pathway §3.2 prioritises (ETV6::RUNX1 + BCR::ABL1 + KMT2A break-apart, then ploidy). RT-PCR substitutes for FISH on several of these; the list has no OR semantics, so the branch that captured an RT-PCR result must declare satisfies_tests: ["Cytogenetics/FISH"] rather than this entry dropping the requirement (DT master §2). Group 1 carries the same code with Flow cytometry in place of IHC — that is a specimen difference (marrow aspirate vs tissue block), not a disagreement.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment (DT master §6; Pathway §2.2, §7.5). C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 (blood, marrow, RES, haematopoietic system NOS) → Group I, Ia1. C42.2 (spleen) and every nodal or extranodal site (C00.0–C41.9, C44.0–C77.9) → Group II, IIb1 — this entry, i.e. B-lymphoblastic lymphoma. Marrow blasts >25% with abnormal peripheral blood resolves to Group I regardless of the nodal mass (Murphy 1980, quoted in Rosolen 2015); ≥5% is Stage IV-BM but stays in Group II. Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side — see presentation_router.json → dual_group_rules['9811-9819'].

morphology_entries.morphology_name: B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma
morphology_entries.nos_fallback_name: Malignant lymphoma, small B lymphocytic, NOS
morphology_entries.coding_note: Small lymphocytic lymphoma — the Group II (nodal) half of a dual-group code whose Group I (leukaemic) half is CLL in Ia2. See topography_routing_note; the clinical_alert is carried verbatim from the Group 1 entry for the same code so the two files cannot drift. Requires the ERIC/ESCCA core panel (CD19, CD5, CD20 dim, CD23, kappa, lambda); borderline cases add CD43, CD79b, CD81, CD200, CD10, ROR1. Retained in the code set despite being adult-only — do not remove.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment (DT master §6). C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 (blood, marrow, RES, haematopoietic system NOS) → Group I, Ia2, i.e. chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. C42.2 (spleen) and every nodal or extranodal site (C00.0–C41.9, C44.0–C77.9) → Group II, IIb2 — this entry, i.e. small lymphocytic lymphoma. Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side — see presentation_router.json → dual_group_rules['9823'].

morphology_entries.coding_note: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. **HTLV-1 serology is the ABSOLUTE gate: without it the code is unassignable and the case falls to 9702, 9700 or 9709** (§3.7, §5.5). Serology is recorded under Molecular/PCR because that is the closest member of this schema's closed test vocabulary — the same convention the Group 1 entry for this code uses; a branch capturing a serology result must declare satisfies_tests: ["Molecular/PCR"]. In a low-prevalence country — which is most of the world outside southwestern Japan, the Caribbean basin, parts of West and Central Africa, and parts of South America — a negative serology is a cheap definitive exclusion and **this code should be near-empty; a populated 9827 warrants review**. Miranda 2024 widens the indication in a way that matters where Hodgkin volume is high: test HTLV-1 in every case suggestive of ATLL AND in **classic Hodgkin lymphoma with atypical background lymphoid cells**, because ATLL can masquerade as CHL. Shimoyama subtyping (acute / lymphomatous / chronic / smouldering) needs blood counts, LDH, calcium, skin examination and nodal status together — the pathology report cannot subtype, and the subtype is code-neutral. The Shimoyama numeric criteria are NOT in this corpus (§8). Primary cutaneous tumoral ATL has been REMOVED from the smouldering group and now requires aggressive treatment. Dual-group — see topography_routing_note.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment (DT master §6; Pathway §7.5). Leukaemic phase (C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4) → Group I, Ia3. Lymphomatous phase, nodal or extranodal (C00.0–C41.9, C42.2, C44.0–C77.9) → Group II, IIb3 — this entry. Shimoyama subtype is recorded as annotation and does not change the code or the group. HTLV-1 serology is mandatory before coding either way. Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side — see presentation_router.json → dual_group_rules['9827'].

morphology_entries.coding_note: T-lineage lymphoblastic disease: surface and/or cytoplasmic CD3, with the required immaturity element (TdT+ and CD1a+, or CD34+ — CD34 is positive in only about a third of T-LL, so CD34− does not exclude) (§3.2). **9729 (precursor T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma) is retired at the tool layer** (contract §1, Pathway §5.4): no morphology_entries object exists for it and every route that would have reached it reaches 9837; the archaic term is retargeted in the alias file. Landing code for ETP-ALL (cCD3+, CD1a <5%, CD8 <5%, CD5 absent-or-dim, ≥1 myeloid/stem marker at ≥25%, MPO <3%) — it has NO separate code. Two hard rules: TdT negative by flow does not exclude T-LBL (reflex to cell-block ICC — 7 of 15 in Bhaker 2015), and cCD3+/sCD3− is a flow phenotype that IHC usually cannot make, so an IHC-only tier cannot fully resolve T-lineage (Cortelazzo 2011). Marrow and CSF were negative and blood counts normal in all 15 of Bhaker's mediastinal cases — a normal haemogram does not argue against T-LBL. Do not hard-code the MPO percentage at the MPAL boundary; proposals run 3% to 28% and no consensus exists (§4.4). Group 1 carries this code with Flow cytometry where this entry names IHC — a specimen difference, not a disagreement.
morphology_entries.topography_routing_note: Dual-group by compartment (DT master §6; Pathway §2.2, §7.5). C42.0/C42.1/C42.3/C42.4 (blood, marrow, RES, haematopoietic system NOS) → Group I, Ia1 (T-ALL). C42.2 (spleen) and every nodal or extranodal site (C00.0–C41.9, C44.0–C77.9) → Group II, IIb1 — this entry, i.e. T-lymphoblastic lymphoma. Marrow blasts >25% with abnormal peripheral blood resolves to Group I regardless of the mediastinal mass. Discriminator is the captured variable `primary_compartment`, asked router-side — see presentation_router.json → dual_group_rules['9811-9819'].

morphology_entries.coding_note: Lymphoproliferative disorder NOS. Family-level terminal for a lymphoid proliferation that is not demonstrably a lymphoma and not demonstrably reactive — and the chain parent for 9971. Ceiling low. The commonest reason to be here is an immune-dysregulation setting (HIV, post-transplant) where §4.5's non-reportable inventory has NOT been excluded: EBV reactivation with preserved architecture, non-destructive PTLD, HIV-associated persistent generalised lymphadenopathy, Castleman disease and IgG4-related disease all belong at the non-reportable terminal, not here. Use this code when a clonal or destructive process is documented but unclassifiable, not as a soft landing for an unexcluded mimic.

Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder NOS. **Tissue biopsy with WHO classification is the gold standard; EBV DNA load is a screening and monitoring tool, NOT a diagnostic one — it cannot on its own reach 9971** (§3.4). Two rules retained at registrar review after Allen 2019 was withdrawn: a material proportion of PTLD is EBV-NEGATIVE, so a negative EBER does not exclude it; and a small number of EBV-positive cells in a graft recipient is not by itself evidence of PTLD. Under ICD-O-3.2 polymorphic PTLD becomes 9971/1 and monomorphic PTLD codes to the specific lymphoma — that behaviour change is NOT applied tonight (contract §1; Pathway §7.6 notes 9971 takes one entry, not a behaviour-split pair). NON-DESTRUCTIVE PTLD is a non-reportable exit (§4.5). Where paediatric solid-organ transplantation is not performed locally, a populated 9971 warrants review before acceptance.

morphology_entries.morphology_name: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma, ALK negative
morphology_entries.coding_note: Systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma with ALK negative by IHC. Term verified against the IARC ICD-O-3.2 table (ICD coding/ICD-O-3.2/icdo32.sqlite, 9715/3 Preferred); breast implant-associated ALCL is a Related term on the same code. Two things the registrar must know. First, 9715 is NOT in the ICCC-2017 IIb3 range (9700-9702,9705,9708,9709,9714,9716-9719,9724-9726,9767,9768) — it falls in the gap between 9714 and 9716, so the ICCC recode returns nothing and the case drops out of Group II unless the range is extended. Second, it is not yet an option in the Group 2 REDCap list. Both are on the to-do list. Clinically: >95% of paediatric ALCL is ALK-positive, so an ALK-negative result in a child is a re-review trigger, not a default. The same IARC table keeps 9714/3 as 'Anaplastic large cell lymphoma, T-cell and Null-cell type' with 'ALK positive' only as a Related term, so the relabelling of 9714 that Changes Made/Aug 2026 proposed is NOT required and is not applied.

Erdheim-Chester disease. Term verified against the IARC ICD-O-3.2 table (9749/3 Preferred, single row). Not in the ICCC-2017 IId range (9740-9742,9750,9751,9754-9759) and not in the Group 2 REDCap list — both on the to-do list. Registered here under registrar ruling 1 of 4 Sep 2026: paediatric occurrence, not the ICCC range, decides whether a code is built. ECD is a disease of middle age (mean 49.6 y) with about twenty documented paediatric cases (mean 9.6 y, youngest 3.5 y), and there is a published proposal that some paediatric CNS juvenile xanthogranuloma carrying BRAF V600E is paediatric ECD. Diagnostic criteria are executable without cross-sectional imaging: plain radiographs of the tibiae and femora showing symmetrical diaphyseal osteosclerosis are an accepted modality. Bilateral leg osteosclerosis is no longer required (5-10% have no bone lesion), foamy histiocytes and Touton cells are not required, S100 is weakly positive in 20-30%. BRAF V600E is present in ~50-69%, is treatment-changing and code-neutral; VE1 IHC alone is not sufficient, so record the assay.

B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with a BCR-ABL1-like (Ph-like) signature, presenting as a lymphoma. Term verified against the IARC ICD-O-3.2 table (9819/3 Preferred) — note the hyphen form BCR-ABL1-like, not BCR::ABL1-like. Registrar ruling 4 of 4 Sep 2026: one code, two groups. The identical entry exists in group_01_dt.json under Ia1 for the leukaemic presentation; ICCC-2017 separates them by topography, restricting 9811-9818 and 9837 away from C42.0 blood, C42.1 marrow and C42.3 RES in Group II and confining them to those sites in Group I. Requires a documented Ph-like signature — CRLF2 rearrangement, an ABL-class fusion or a JAK-STAT lesion — by FISH or RNA-seq, with BCR::ABL1 itself negative. About 15% of childhood ALL, rising through adolescence. Not in the ICCC-2017 IIb1 range (9811-9818,9837) and not in the Group 2 REDCap list, though it IS already in the Group 1 REDCap list. Both gaps are on the to-do list.

decision_trees.tree_label: Nodal / extranodal lymphoma — the main lymphoid spine

nodes.question: What specimen and what reports are actually in this patient's file? Pick the highest tier available, or the outcome state that applies to the aspirate.
nodes.hint: This is the specimen ladder (Pathway §2.4). It fixes what precision is achievable. An FNA has FOUR outcome states — adequate and positive, adequate and negative, inadequate, and not done. Inadequate is not a negative.
nodes.coding_note: Fixation is an upstream gate: with unbuffered formalin or fixation beyond 72 h, CD10 falls to 17%, Ki-67 >90% to 24% and MYC FISH signal to 3%. Record fixation quality before offering any IHC- or FISH-tier route (Emile 2016, Pathway §2.4).

options.label: Referral or clinical note only — no cytology and no histology report
options.coding_note: Tier 1. The referral diagnosis was wrong or uncertain in 57% of NLPHL cases and clinically diagnosed Burkitt was confirmed in only 75% (Xia 2022, Ogwang 2011).

options.label: FNA smear only — ADEQUATE, and the cytology reports a neoplastic / malignant / lymphomatous population (no cell block, no flow, no IHC)
options.coding_note: Adequate-positive. FNAC alone cannot carry a lineage-specific code: PPV for an FNAC call of 'NHL' is 71.4% and FNAC misses about 1 in 5 Hodgkin lymphomas (Alemu 2026).

options.label: FNA smear only — ADEQUATE, and the cytology reports granulomas, necrosis, reactive change or another benign picture
options.coding_note: Adequate-negative. FNA separates TB from reactive at 98.3% specificity, but a granulomatous node is neither a TB diagnosis nor an exclusion of lymphoma (Pathway §2.3).

options.label: FNA smear only — INADEQUATE / non-diagnostic ("too few cells for cytology")
options.coding_note: Paediatric insufficiency rate 8/173 (5%), Richardson 2021. A special investigation changed or added the diagnosis in 4 of those 8.

options.label: FNA smear only — technically UNINTERPRETABLE (air-dried, obscured by blood, stain failure); no opinion could be given on the cells present
options.coding_note: Not assessable. Distinct from inadequate (too few cells) and from a benign result. Both route to repeat-or-escalate; neither may close to an NOS malignant code.

options.label: FNA + cell block, or core needle biopsy, or excisional / incisional biopsy — H&E only, no IHC and no flow
options.coding_note: Tier 2. WHO-HAEM5's own rule governs: where resources or specimen quality are insufficient for an entity, apply the family-level label.

options.label: Tissue (cell block / core / excisional) WITH immunohistochemistry and/or flow cytometry
options.coding_note: Tier 3. Excision is still required for FL grade, composite lymphoma (9596), THRLBL vs NLPHL architecture and NLPHL nodularity — a core cannot settle those (Ingersoll 2019, Ding 2024, Xia 2022).

options.label: Effusion, CSF, marrow aspirate or node aspirate WITH flow cytometry — no tissue block
options.coding_note: Full flow phenotyping including the Burkitt signature and T-LBL is reachable on these specimens (Tsagarakis 2020, Bhaker 2015). Marrow and CSF were negative in all 15 of Bhaker's T-LBL cases and blood counts were normal in all — a normal haemogram does not argue against T-LBL.

options.label: Tissue with IHC/flow PLUS cytogenetics / FISH, or plus molecular / NGS
options.coding_note: Tier 4–5. Where one FISH test is affordable, run it on the FNA cell block — hybridisation failure ~1% and MYC/BCL2 concordance with excision was 100% across 34 paired specimens (Menke 2024).

options.label: Malignancy excluded on review — reactive, infective or non-neoplastic; or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: The wording chooses the code, and nothing above the family level is reachable from a referral. Do not read a named entity out of a referral note.
nodes.coding_note: Tier 1 achieves only 9590, 9591 and 9650 (Pathway §2.5). Confidence is LOW and every downstream test is an upgrade. Record why the case is NOS via workup_status.

options.label: Note reads "lymphoma" or "malignant lymphoma" — Hodgkin vs non-Hodgkin not stated
options.upgrade_path: H&E morphology would separate Hodgkin from non-Hodgkin (9650 vs 9591). IHC would give lineage and most entities.

options.label: Note reads "non-Hodgkin lymphoma" or "NHL" — no subtype stated
options.upgrade_path: IHC on tissue would give the lineage and in most cases the entity.
options.coding_note: 9591 is the only restricted-band code permitted to carry C80.9 unknown primary.

options.label: Note reads "Hodgkin lymphoma" or "Hodgkin's disease" — no subtype and no pathology report
options.upgrade_path: H&E plus CD30 / CD15 / CD20 / PAX5 would give the CHL subtype, or separate NLPHL (9659) from lymphocyte-rich CHL (9651).

options.label: Note names a specific entity — "Burkitt", "DLBCL", "T-cell lymphoma" — but no pathology report is in the file
options.upgrade_path: Tissue with IHC would confirm or refute the named entity. Burkitt additionally needs BCL2, Ki-67 and TdT, and ideally MYC FISH.
options.coding_note: Do not code the named entity from a referral. 9591 is the honest ceiling. Record the referral wording verbatim so the case can be re-coded when pathology arrives.

options.label: Note reads only "lymphadenopathy", "neck mass for investigation" or similar — no diagnosis asserted
options.coding_note: This is not a lymphoma referral. It must go through the not-lymphoma gate before any code is considered.

nodes.question: The aspirate was adequate and the cytology calls it neoplastic. What exactly does the cytology report say?
nodes.hint: No cell block means no IHC, no flow and no FISH — so no lineage-specific code. Against histology, FNAC runs 92.1% accurate overall but PPV 80.9%.
nodes.coding_note: Malignancy risk rises with ≥2 nodal regions (AOR 4.32) and non-cervical site (AOR 2.07). Prior lymphoma history raises FNA/CNB definitiveness from 71% to 95.4% (OR 8.52) — age, sex, symptoms, biopsy site and guidance modality do not, so do not ask about them.

options.label: Cytology reads "non-Hodgkin lymphoma" or "lymphomatous population"
options.upgrade_path: A cell block would allow IHC (CD20, CD3, CD30, Ki-67, TdT, BCL2, CD10) and reach the entity. On a cell block, FISH failure is only ~1%.
options.coding_note: PPV of an FNAC call of 'NHL' is 71.4%, with a 27% false-positive rate. 9591 is the ceiling — do not read a subtype out of a smear.

options.label: Cytology reads "Hodgkin lymphoma" — Reed-Sternberg-like cells described on the smear
options.upgrade_path: Excisional biopsy with CD30, CD15, PAX5, CD20, MUM1 and EBER would give the subtype and separate NLPHL, THRLBL and lymphocyte-rich CHL.

options.label: Cytology reads "neoplastic" / "suspicious for malignancy" — lineage or type not stated
options.coding_note: Tier 1 only. In a child this is a referral for tissue. Do not close it to an NOS lymphoma code from this node.

options.label: Cytology reads "metastatic carcinoma", "small round blue cell tumour" or another non-lymphoid malignancy
options.coding_note: Metastasis on FNA has PPV 100% (Alemu 2026), but this is not a Group II diagnosis. Escalate to tissue and code from the correct group's tree.

options.label: Cytology reads granulomatous, necrotising or reactive — no neoplastic population after all

nodes.question: The aspirate cannot close this case. What happened next?
nodes.hint: This node exists so that an inadequate or uninterpretable aspirate is never resolved to a malignant NOS code. It closes only when a further specimen exists, or when the record shows there will not be one.
nodes.coding_note: Richardson 2021: repeat FNAB confirmed M. tuberculosis in 2 cytologically suspected cases, and a special investigation (chest X-ray, respiratory culture, Xpert) changed or added the diagnosis in 8/173 including 4 of the 8 non-diagnostic aspirates. Keep the aspirate open, do not close it to 9590.

options.label: A repeat FNA or a tissue biopsy is now in the file — go back and enter it
options.coding_note: Re-enter at the evidence gate with the new specimen. Do not carry the inadequate result forward.

options.label: A repeat aspirate or special investigation confirmed mycobacterial disease
Tissue biopsy WITH IHC is now available
The aspirate was ADEQUATE and called neoplastic, no further specimen is obtainable, and the treating team has closed the case as a lymphoma on clinical and cytological grounds
options.upgrade_path: A cell block or tissue biopsy with IHC would give lineage and entity. Recorded as a permanent no-tissue terminal at this facility.
options.coding_note: Reachable ONLY from an adequate, positive aspirate. An inadequate or uninterpretable aspirate must never resolve here (Pathway §2.4).

options.label: The aspirate was INADEQUATE or uninterpretable and no further specimen exists — patient lost to follow-up, died before biopsy, or biopsy declined
options.reason: No diagnostic specimen was ever obtained, so a malignancy was never established. An inadequate aspirate must not be coded 9590 — 5% of paediatric FNABs are non-diagnostic and 2 of 11 such cases proved mycobacterial on later biopsy. Record the reason the specimen was never obtained and re-enter the tool if tissue arrives.

options.label: Review concluded there is no malignancy — infective, reactive or non-neoplastic
options.reason: Reviewed as non-neoplastic after escalation. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: What does the H&E report describe? No IHC has been done.
nodes.hint: H&E reaches the family level and no further — Hodgkin vs non-Hodgkin, and the architectural pattern. Do not read an entity out of morphology alone.
nodes.coding_note: WHO-HAEM5's own rule: where resources or specimen quality are insufficient for an entity, apply the family-level label. That is exactly this tier (Pathway §2.5).

options.label: Reed-Sternberg or Hodgkin-like cells in an inflammatory background
options.upgrade_path: CD30, CD15, PAX5, CD20, MUM1/IRF4 and EBER would give the CHL subtype and separate NLPHL (9659), THRLBL (9688) and lymphocyte-rich CHL (9651).

options.label: Starry-sky pattern with monotonous intermediate-sized cells and multiple small basophilic nucleoli
options.upgrade_path: CD20, BCL2, Ki-67 and TdT would reach 9687 — Burkitt needs BCL2 negative, Ki-67 ≥90% and TdT negative. MYC break-apart FISH is the entity-defining test.
options.coding_note: Starry sky on H&E alone does not reach 9687 — it is a pattern, not a phenotype, and B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with MYC rearrangement is an exact mimic that must never be coded 9687 (Pathway §3.3).

options.label: Diffuse infiltrate of large atypical lymphoid cells
options.upgrade_path: CD20, CD3, CD30 and ALK would give lineage; CD10, BCL6, MUM1, CD138 and LANA-1 would give the entity.
options.coding_note: 9591 rather than 9680 — 'large B-cell' is a phenotype and no B-cell marker has been read yet.

options.label: Blastic / lymphoblastic morphology — a monotonous population of small-to-medium cells with fine chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli
options.upgrade_path: TdT plus CD34 and a B/T panel (CD19, CD22, cCD79a, PAX5 vs cCD3) would reach 9727, 9811 or 9837. TdT on a cell block is the single most valuable stain here.
options.coding_note: 9727 requires TdT. Do not emit it from H&E alone. TdT negative by flow does not exclude T-LBL — it was flow-negative in 7 of 15 cases and cell-block immunocytochemistry positive in all seven (Bhaker 2015).

options.label: Nodular or follicular architecture with atypical follicles
options.upgrade_path: CD20, CD10, BCL6, BCL2 and Ki-67 would separate follicular lymphoma from a reactive or paediatric-type process. Grading requires an excisional biopsy.

options.label: IHC has since been performed — go on to the compartment gate
Granulomatous or necrotising granulomatous inflammation, with or without an atypical population
options.coding_note: Granulomas have the lowest specificity of any test in this gate (sens 83%). A granulomatous node is neither a TB diagnosis nor an exclusion of lymphoma.

options.label: Preserved nodal architecture — follicular hyperplasia, sinus histiocytosis or another reactive pattern
Reviewed — no malignant lymphoid population; the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: H&E review found no malignant lymphoid population and the diagnosis was revised. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: What does the bone marrow show? This decides whether the case belongs to Group II at all.
nodes.hint: Group II's equivalent of site resolution. The requirement is bilateral marrow aspirates plus a biopsy. Tick 'no marrow done' rather than guessing — the split is then provisional and must be recorded as such.
nodes.coding_note: Nine codes (9811–9818, 9837, 9823, 9827) are topography-restricted away from C42.0 blood, C42.1 marrow and C42.3 RES; C42.2 spleen is re-admitted. The sqlite enforces the result, the blast count produces it. Config key group_i_ii_blast_boundary. nos_fallback is null by node type — the non-resolving path continues rather than terminating (Pathway §7.3).

options.descriptor: No marrow examination in the file
options.coding_note: The gate cannot be closed. Code at tissue tier and flag marrow_not_done — the Group I / Group II split is provisional until a marrow is done.

options.descriptor: Marrow done — lymphoma cells less than 5% of the aspirate
options.coding_note: Group II, and not Stage IV.

options.descriptor: Marrow done — lymphoma cells 5% or more but not above 25% on aspirate morphology
options.coding_note: Group II, Stage IV-BM. Stays in this group.

options.descriptor: Marrow blasts above 25% AND the peripheral blood is abnormal (blasts on the film, cytopenias, leukocytosis)
options.reason: Marrow blasts above 25% with an abnormal peripheral blood film place this case in Group I (leukaemias), not Group II. Code it from the Group I acute-leukaemia tree. Record the exact marrow blast percentage and the blood film findings — the boundary comes from Murphy 1980, quoted in Rosolen 2015, and is the single most load-bearing rule in this group.

options.descriptor: Marrow blasts above 25% but the peripheral blood is normal, or the blood film is not documented
options.coding_note: Stays in Group II pending the blood film. Do not refer to Group I on the marrow percentage alone.

options.descriptor: Marrow positive only by immunophenotype, FISH or PCR (BMi / BMc / BMmol) — negative on aspirate morphology
options.coding_note: Do NOT upstage. Keep the assigned stage and record the modifier (Pathway §2.2).

options.descriptor: Marrow shows a blastoid infiltrate distending the sinuses, with dyspoietic haematopoiesis

nodes.question: Before any lymphoma code: does the file establish a non-malignant explanation, or is a malignant lymphoid population actually present?
nodes.hint: In a TB- and HIV-endemic lymphadenopathy population the pre-test mix is roughly 52% tuberculous lymphadenitis, 30% reactive and 9% lymphoma. This gate is load-bearing, not a formality.
nodes.coding_note: Authored as a document_inventory rather than the ihc_checklist sketched in Pathway §7.2. It is a gate, not a refining node, and an ihc_checklist would force a non-null NOS fallback — falling back to 'lymphoma NOS' when the TB workup is inconclusive is exactly the over-call this gate exists to prevent. Deviation recorded in G2_OPEN_ITEMS.md. Forcing an NOS malignant code here records a cancer that does not exist (Pathway §4.5).

options.label: Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra POSITIVE (on FNA or tissue) and NO malignant lymphoid population is described
options.reason: Tuberculous lymphadenitis. Xpert Ultra on FNA has specificity 100% and PPV 100% in this setting. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. Re-enter the tool if a subsequent biopsy shows a malignant population, because dual TB and lymphoma occurs.

options.label: Xpert Ultra POSITIVE and a malignant lymphoid population IS described
Xpert Ultra TRACE-positive — morphology not malignant
options.coding_note: A trace result is suspect (2 of 12 were false positives). Neither a TB diagnosis nor an exclusion of lymphoma. Repeat on a core biopsy.

options.label: Xpert Ultra NEGATIVE or not done, granulomas present, no malignant population
options.coding_note: Ultra-negative does not exclude TB (NPV 83–87%). AFB smear (sens 26%) and culture (sens 33–39%) are not to be relied on. Proceed to core biopsy; repeat Ultra on the core if granulomas persist.

options.label: Reactive follicular hyperplasia — preserved architecture, polytypic B cells, no atypical population
options.reason: Reactive follicular hyperplasia. Around 30% of this population's lymphadenopathy is reactive. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

options.label: HIV-associated persistent generalised lymphadenopathy
options.reason: HIV-associated persistent generalised lymphadenopathy is not a neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. Record hiv_status; HIV raises the risk of several Group II entities and the case should be re-entered if a mass develops.

options.label: Progressive transformation of germinal centres — mantle-zone-expanded follicles, IgD+ rim, no LP cells, PD-1 / CD57-rich background
options.reason: Progressive transformation of germinal centres is not neoplastic. Increased follicular-helper T cells alone must never be coded 9659, and PTGC frequently coexists with, precedes or follows nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma — re-enter the tool if LP cells are demonstrated on review or on a later biopsy.

options.label: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease — histiocytic necrotising lymphadenitis with karyorrhectic debris and absent neutrophils
options.reason: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease is a self-limiting non-neoplastic lymphadenitis. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

options.label: Infectious mononucleosis, or EBV reactivation with preserved nodal architecture
options.reason: Infectious mononucleosis or EBV reactivation with preserved architecture. EBER-positive cells in a node with intact architecture are not evidence of lymphoma, and a small number of EBV-positive cells in a graft recipient is not by itself evidence of PTLD. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

options.label: Castleman disease — hyaline-vascular or plasma-cell type, no HHV-8-positive plasmablasts
options.reason: Castleman disease without an HHV-8-positive large B-cell proliferation is not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. If HHV-8 LANA-1 has not been done in a multicentric case, order it before closing.

options.label: Multicentric Castleman disease WITH HHV-8 LANA-1-positive plasmablasts
IgG4-related disease — storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis, raised IgG4+ plasma cells and serum IgG4
options.reason: IgG4-related disease is an immune-mediated fibro-inflammatory condition, not a neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

options.label: Indolent T-lymphoblastic proliferation — TdT-positive cells that distort but do not obliterate the architecture, less atypical than lymphoblasts, no monoclonal TCR
options.reason: Indolent T-lymphoblastic proliferation is a tumour-like lesion, not a lymphoblastic lymphoma. It must not be coded 9727 or 9837 — this is a hard false-positive guard (Pathway §3.2). Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

options.label: In situ follicular neoplasia, or in situ mantle cell neoplasia — an incidental finding in an otherwise reactive node
options.reason: In situ follicular neoplasia and in situ mantle cell neoplasia are incidental low-risk lesions and must not be registered as systemic lymphoma (Pathway §3.5). Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

options.label: Non-destructive post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder — plasmacytic hyperplasia, infectious-mononucleosis-like, or florid follicular hyperplasia with preserved architecture
options.reason: Non-destructive PTLD preserves the nodal architecture and is not registered as a lymphoma. EBV DNA load is a screening and monitoring tool, not a diagnostic one, and cannot on its own reach 9971. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. Re-enter the tool if a polymorphic or monomorphic PTLD develops.

options.label: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis — no neoplastic population on an adequate specimen
options.reason: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, primary or secondary, has no ICD-O-3 code and is not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. Record it as a named uncoded entity.

options.label: Haemophagocytosis WITH an atypical lymphoid or CD30-positive population identified
A malignant lymphoid population is present and the mimics above have been considered — continue to lineage
options.coding_note: Once TB is excluded the population inverts: among 63 non-TB patients, 38% had lymphoma and 19% disseminated malignancy (Antel).

nodes.question: What does the immunohistochemistry report say? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: Lineage first, entity second. TdT separates precursor from mature; CD30 with dim PAX5 and absent CD45 separates classic Hodgkin from everything else.
nodes.coding_note: Lineage assignment thresholds (Pathway §4.4): B = strong CD19 plus ≥1 strong CD10/CD22/CD79a, or weak CD19 plus ≥2 of those; T = cCD3 or sCD3 with intensity in part exceeding 50% of mature T cells; myeloid = MPO intensity in part exceeding 50% of mature neutrophils, or ≥2 of NSE/CD11c/CD14/CD64/lysozyme. TCR and IGH clonality must NEVER be used for lineage assignment (Duffield 2022). CD3 is absent in more than 75% of ALCL — CD3-negativity does not exclude a T-cell lymphoma.

markers: CD45 negative on the large cells

marker_groups.group_label: Myeloid — read only to exclude a mixed phenotype
Clinical and site context (tick if documented)

resolution_logic.reason: Two lineages are met on the same blast population — mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia. MPAL has no Group II code. Code this from the Group I acute-leukaemia tree. Record the MPO percentage and the method used (cytochemistry or flow): proposals range from 3% to 28%, >10% improves specificity, and no consensus threshold exists, so the number and the method must both be on the record.

No lineage-defining marker was found — acute undifferentiated leukaemia or acute leukaemia of ambiguous lineage. Neither has a Group II code. Code this from the Group I acute-leukaemia tree, where the panel-adequacy rules for AUL versus ALAL-NOS are carried.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Cutaneous presentations must not be forced down the nodal flow (Pathway §7.1). The cutaneous tree carries mycosis fungoides, Sézary syndrome, the CD30+ lymphoproliferative behaviour split, hydroa vacciniforme-like disease, the primary cutaneous gamma-delta entity and the 9709 entity boundary.

ICC reverses the 2016 WHO rule: a TdT-positive high-grade or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma must NOT be reclassified as lymphoblastic — report it as a mature lymphoma with TdT expression noted. This rule must be tested before the TdT/CD34 precursor rule below or it never fires (Pathway §3.2, §5.3).
Tested before the Hodgkin rules deliberately. A positive HTLV-1 serology in a Hodgkin-like node re-routes the case to the mature T tree, where 9827 is resolved.

negative: CD45 negative on the large cells

resolution_logic.coding_note: LP cells reach the Hodgkin node even though nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma is CD20-positive — the NLPHL / THRLBL / lymphocyte-rich CHL triangle is resolved there together.

Immaturity is a required element, not optional. The precursor node applies it: B-lineage needs TdT plus CD34, or bright CD10 with low CD45, low/absent CD20 and absent surface Ig; T-lineage needs TdT plus CD1a, or CD34 (positive in only about a third of T-LBL, so CD34-negative does not exclude).

Light-chain restriction establishes a B-cell clone. It does not establish lineage in a nodal TFH lymphoma, where clonal IGH/IGK occurs in about 30% of cases and must not re-route the case to a B-cell code (Pathway §3.7).

A CD30-positive large-cell tumour without B markers and without CD15 is anaplastic large cell lymphoma until ALK is read. Miranda 2024: run ALK immunostaining on every T-cell lymphoma with even a minor CD30-positive component.
Mast cell presentations must not be forced down the nodal flow. The mast cell tree carries the harmonized 2024 criteria and the ≥20% smear count for mast cell leukaemia.
CD163 is the first-listed required marker of the Goyal 2026 minimum panel and the marker most routine lymphoma panels omit.
CD1a alone is insufficient — it mistakes an indeterminate dendritic cell tumour for Langerhans cell histiocytosis. The histiocytic tree reads CD163, CD1a, CD207 and S100 together.
Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is the most likely under-ascertained code in this group because CD21/CD23/CD35 are not in routine panels. Clusterin has 100% sensitivity and 93% specificity.

nos_fallback.name: Malignant lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A malignant lymphoid population is present but no lineage-defining marker combination was met. 9590 is the family-level label WHO-HAEM5 itself sanctions when the panel cannot reach an entity.

order: CD45 negative on the large cells

nodes.question: This node resolves the NLPHL / THRLBL / lymphocyte-rich CHL triangle before it subtypes classic Hodgkin lymphoma. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: The three corners differ by the BACKGROUND, not by the large cells: small B cells present or absent, FDC meshwork expanded-and-fragmented or compact-and-intact or absent, CD4>CD8 or CD8>CD4. Flow cytometry is useless here — the phenotypes are nearly identical.
nodes.coding_note: CHL subtyping is unchanged from WHO-HAEM4R in both classifications and should still be coded — the subtypes have lost prognostic weight but are retained for epidemiology. Standard panel: CD30, CD15, IRF4/MUM1, PAX5, CD20, CD3 plus LMP1 or EBER ISH. Keep 9659 in IIa; ICC's 'nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma' is a synonym, not a re-grouping (Pathway §5.3).

markers: CD30 weak or partial in LP cells

marker_groups.group_label: The background — this is what decides the corner
markers: Residual nodules or loose LP-cell clusters in a diffuse area
Mantle-zone-expanded follicles with an IgD+ rim, no LP cells
EBER positive in the large cells
EBER negative with a passing control probe

prior_probability.interpretation: NLPHL is EBV-negative regardless of geography — pooled 4% (23/630), LMIC 7% vs HIC 3%, not significant, and 0/18 Kenyan cases had EBER-positive LP cells. A positive EBER in LP-type cells is therefore strongly discriminating and a reason to re-review, unlike in classic Hodgkin lymphoma (overall 40%, mixed cellularity 70–80%, HIV-related >90%) where a positive result is expected and weakly informative. Pre-2000 reports of high EBV in 'lymphocyte-predominant HL' conflated 9659 with 9651 and must not be used.

positive: Mantle-zone-expanded follicles with an IgD+ rim, no LP cells
resolution_logic.reason: Progressive transformation of germinal centres — mantle-zone-expanded follicles with an IgD-positive rim, no LP cells, PD-1/CD57-rich background. This is not neoplastic and increased follicular-helper T cells alone must never be coded 9659. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Tested before every classic Hodgkin rule. Serology is cheap and the misclassification is real (Miranda 2024).

positive: EBER positive in the large cells
resolution_logic.coding_note: Tested before the CHL rules. In an HIV or immune-dysregulation setting this is the commonest way a CHL diagnosis is wrong.

positive: Residual nodules or loose LP-cell clusters in a diffuse area
resolution_logic.coding_note: Fan pattern E. A diffuse THRLBL-like area with focal residual nodules, loose LP-cell clusters on CD20/OCT2, a few residual small B cells, or traces of FDC meshwork is 9659, NOT 9688. This rule is deliberately tested before the THRLBL rule below (Pathway §3.1).

positive: CD30 weak or partial in LP cells
resolution_logic.coding_note: CD30 weak or variable in LP-type cells with OCT2 strong is still 9659. In the Kenyan series CD30 was positive in a subset of LP cells in 1 of 21 and CD15 in 2 of 21 — neither converts the code. CD30-positive immunoblasts in the background (4 of 21) are not LP cells and must not be read as 9651. Tested before every CD30 rule.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: An excisional biopsy with CD21/CD23 to show the FDC meshwork pattern, background small B cells and the CD4/CD8 ratio would separate 9659 (IIa) from 9688 (IIb2). A core biopsy cannot.
resolution_logic.coding_note: The two candidates sit in different ICCC-3 subgroups, so neither 9650 nor 9680 is honest here. 9590 is the family-level label until an excision is available (Pathway §2.4).

T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma: CD20-positive large cells, NO background small B cells, NO FDC meshwork, background CD8 > CD4, no PD-1 rosettes. All three negatives are required — check that the Fan pattern E rule above did not apply first.

LP cells CD20+, CD79a+, PAX5+ (weaker than background B), OCT2 strong, BOB1+, PU.1+, BCL6+, CD45+, MUM1−, CD10−; expanded fragmented irregular FDC meshwork; PD-1 rosettes; background CD4 > CD8. Newer tiebreakers: Fascin negative, GATA3 negative, MEF2B positive, light-chain restriction demonstrable.

Lymphocyte-rich classic Hodgkin lymphoma: HRS cells with CD30 strong and homogeneous, CD15 variable, MUM1 strong, PAX5 dim, CD20/CD79a negative or variable, against a compact intact FDC meshwork around eccentric regressed germinal centres. Fascin and/or GATA3 positive (± STAT6) support it over NLPHL.
Classic Hodgkin lymphoma confirmed on phenotype. The subtype is an architectural call and is made at the next node.

nos_fallback.name: Hodgkin lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Hodgkin lymphoma established but the panel did not resolve the corner of the triangle or the classic subtype.

EBER positive in the large cells
CD30 weak or partial in LP cells

nodes.question: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma confirmed. Which architectural pattern does the report describe?
nodes.hint: Architecture, not phenotype, decides the subtype. If the report does not state a pattern, say so — do not infer one from the clinical stage or the site.
nodes.coding_note: Retained for epidemiology even though the subtypes have lost prognostic weight. Nodular sclerosis grading (British National Lymphoma Investigation grades 1 and 2) is optional — record it only where the report states it. Hodgkin granuloma (9661) and Hodgkin sarcoma (9662) are archaic synonyms of mixed cellularity and lymphocyte depletion respectively and are handled by the alias file, not by this node.

options.descriptor: Nodular sclerosis — collagen bands, lacunar cells, nodular growth; grade not stated
Nodular sclerosis, cellular phase — nodularity and lacunar cells with little or no collagen
Nodular sclerosis, grade 1 (BNLI) — the report explicitly states grade 1
options.coding_note: Record classification_used. Grading nodular sclerosis is optional in both current classifications.

options.descriptor: Nodular sclerosis, grade 2 (BNLI) — the report explicitly states grade 2 or 'syncytial variant'
options.coding_note: Record classification_used.

options.descriptor: Mixed cellularity — diffuse or vaguely nodular, mixed inflammatory background, no sclerosis
Lymphocyte depletion — subtype of depletion not further specified
Lymphocyte depletion, diffuse fibrosis type — hypocellular, disordered fibrosis, few HRS cells
Lymphocyte depletion, reticular type — sheets of pleomorphic HRS cells
Both a Hodgkin and a non-Hodgkin component are demonstrated in the SAME excisional specimen
options.coding_note: Composite Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Requires an excisional biopsy — the two components must both be demonstrated, not inferred. Record both component diagnoses as free text.

options.descriptor: Architecture not stated in the report, or the specimen is a core biopsy and the pattern cannot be assessed
options.upgrade_path: An excisional biopsy would give the architectural pattern and the subtype (9663, 9652, 9653–9655 or 9651).
options.coding_note: 9650 is the honest terminal when the pattern is not stated. Do not infer nodular sclerosis from a mediastinal mass in an adolescent.

options.descriptor: On review this is not Hodgkin lymphoma — the large cells are B-lineage with a strong uniform B-cell programme
options.coding_note: An EBV-positive lesion with a strong uniform B-cell programme is EBV-positive DLBCL, not CHL (Pathway §3.1).

prior_probability.expected_positive_pct: 40 overall; 70-80 in mixed cellularity; >90 in HIV-related disease
prior_probability.interpretation: EBER positivity is expected across classic Hodgkin lymphoma and is therefore weakly informative here — it neither confirms nor refines the subtype. It discriminates only against **nodular lymphocyte predominance (9659), where EBER is positive in under 4%**. Record the result; do not let it change the subtype.

nodes.question: B lineage confirmed and TdT is not driving the case. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: Order matters here. The two Burkitt mimics are tested first, then the plasmablastic family, then the large-cell entities, then the small-B and follicular routes. Ki-67, BCL2 and CD10 are the three that do most of the work.
nodes.coding_note: MYC IHC is NOT a FISH surrogate: in the 30–50% band the result is unusable, nearly a third of cases sit there, inter-method concordance is 50–60%, and on core biopsies there is no significant association with MYC rearrangement at all. Dual-expressor pre-selection at 40% misses ~35% of HGBL-DH. Record myc_ihc_pct and myc_scoring_method; never let MYC IHC stand in for FISH (Pathway §3.3).

markers: CD20 negative on the tumour cells
Fibrous background with clear or retracted cytoplasm
EBER positive in >80% of viable tumour cells
EBER positive in a minority of cells
EBER negative with a passing control probe
EBER counted per high-power field (lymphomatoid granulomatosis grading)

prior_probability.interpretation: Expected EBER positivity is ~100% in endemic Burkitt, ~90% in Arboleda's African cohort (only 1 negative of 52), 10–80% sporadic and 30–40% AIDS-associated. A positive result is therefore expected and weakly informative; an EBER-NEGATIVE endemic-pattern case is a reason to reconsider the diagnosis. Elsewhere in this node the priors differ sharply: DLBCL NOS 10%, HIV-related DLBCL 20–60%, plasmablastic 75–90%, primary effusion lymphoma 75–90%, post-transplant and HIV-related B-LPD >90%.

marker_groups.group_label: Clinical and site context (tick if documented)
markers: Localised head-and-neck or Waldeyer's-ring mass, stage I–II
Skin-limited lesion on head or trunk
Large B cells confined to vascular lumina

Cytogenetics / FISH report is in the file

resolution_logic.coding_note: Both ICC and WHO route this entity to the B-lymphoblastic range (9811–9818). Tested before every Burkitt rule (Pathway §3.3, §5.2).

positive: CD20 negative on the tumour cells
resolution_logic.coding_note: A CD20-negative, CD138-positive tumour is the plasmablastic family. Four codes are separated by three stains and every one of them is hard-gated on a viral or ALK result.

positive: CD20 negative on the tumour cells
EBER positive in a minority of cells
resolution_logic.coding_note: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis. The ICD-O-3 name — Angiocentric immunoproliferative lesion — is archaic and no clerk will recognise it; it is handled by the alias file and the name is NOT edited here. Grade by EBER-positive cells per high-power field: grade 1 <5, grade 2 5–20, grade 3 >50 and often >100. EBER is seen in only about half of grade 1 lesions, so a negative EBER on a grade-1-looking lesion means re-biopsy, not exclusion. ICD-O-3 has no grade modifier, so record eber_per_hpf; grade may change in either direction on re-biopsy without a new primary. Under ICC 2022 a CNS- or GI-only EBV-positive LYG-like lesion is no longer LYG.

Nodal or marrow involvement is a hard exclusion for lymphomatoid granulomatosis — reconsider the diagnosis. An EBV-positive angiocentric large B-cell process with nodal or marrow disease codes as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Pathway §3.4).

positive: Large B cells confined to vascular lumina
resolution_logic.coding_note: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. The diagnosis rests on the intravascular distribution, not on the phenotype.

Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma. Donzel 2023 (n=49): fibrous background with clear or retracted cytoplasm, Hodgkin-like cells in 65%, BCL6+ 96%, MUM1+ 82%, CD30+ 88%, CD23+ 75%. CD23 is the discriminating marker most panels lack. Paediatric mature B-cell lymphoma runs Burkitt → germinal-centre DLBCL → PMBCL in descending frequency, so PMBCL is the least likely of the three overall but the most likely once the mass is anterior mediastinal and the patient adolescent — the site and age do the work, not the base rate (Goldman & Cairo 2023).

positive: High tumour-cell density with ≥2 strongly expressed B-cell markers, mediastinal
resolution_logic.coding_note: Mediastinal gray zone lymphoma — mapped to 9596 by convention only (Pathway §5.2). ICC's rule: mediastinal plus high tumour-cell density plus ≥2 strongly expressed B-cell markers. Nodular-sclerosis CHL with variable CD20 remains CHL, and gray-zone morphology OUTSIDE the mediastinum is 9680.

Coded 9687 because the 11q entity has no ICD-O-3 code, but flagged as provisional rather than absorbed silently. 11q is defined by 11q23.2–23.3 gain PLUS telomeric loss at 11q24.1-qter — gain alone is non-specific and insufficient.

provisional_pending.reason: LMO2-positive Burkitt-like morphology. MYC status unknown; HG/LBCL-11q and HGBL-DH not excluded.
alternative_entities: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements

positive: Cytogenetics / FISH report is in the file
resolution_logic.coding_note: Burkitt phenotype with a FISH report available — resolve MYC before terminating. Sequential algorithm: MYC break-apart first (accept a 5–10% miss rate), then BCL2 and BCL6 only if MYC is rearranged; if MYC-negative and the morphology fits Burkitt, test 11q.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: MYC break-apart FISH on the cell block would confirm the entity and exclude the two mimics. Failure rate ~1%, and MYC/BCL2 concordance with excision was 100% across 34 paired specimens.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Route 1 of the four validated no-FISH routes to 9687 (Arboleda 2021, n=52, 83% paediatric: CD20 100%, CD10 79.2%, BCL6 87.9%, BCL2 weak-focal in only 6.4%, Ki-67 mean 96%). Absence of MYC does not exclude Burkitt — some morphologically and phenotypically typical cases show no MYC rearrangement.

provisional_pending.reason: MYC status unknown; HG/LBCL-11q and HGBL-DH not excluded.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: MYC break-apart FISH on the cell block would confirm the entity and exclude the two mimics.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Burkitt morphology plus CD20 plus BCL2-negative plus Ki-67 ≥90% plus TdT-negative. Chamba's phase-1 tissue panel (BCL2, CD10, CD20) alone gives 81% concordance with WHO standard-of-care pathology.

provisional_pending.reason: MYC status unknown; HG/LBCL-11q and HGBL-DH not excluded.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Repeat EBER ISH with a passing control probe (U6) — the control failed, so the EBV status of this tumour is unknown, not negative. MYC break-apart FISH would separately confirm the entity.
resolution_logic.coding_note: An EBER negative WITHOUT a passing control is 'not assessable', never negative (Pathway §4.3). This branch deliberately does not carry the reconsider-the-diagnosis alert that a true EBER-negative endemic-pattern case carries — the test did not run.

provisional_pending.reason: MYC status unknown; HG/LBCL-11q and HGBL-DH not excluded. EBER control failed, so EBV status is unestablished.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: MYC break-apart FISH would confirm the entity. Consider re-review of the morphology and phenotype before the code is finalised.

provisional_pending.reason: MYC status unknown; HG/LBCL-11q and HGBL-DH not excluded.

positive: Localised head-and-neck or Waldeyer's-ring mass, stage I–II
resolution_logic.coding_note: Routed to the follicular node, which carries the paediatric-lesion guards and the IRF4 FISH route. IRF4 rearrangement is cryptic in ~10% and the entity has no ICD-O-3 code.
Splenic marginal zone B-cell lymphoma. C42.2 spleen is explicitly re-admitted to the Group II topography ranges.

MNDA and IRTA1 favour marginal zone over follicular when CD10 is negative and BCL2 ambiguous. In a child, check the paediatric nodal MZL guard at the follicular node first — pNMZL belongs to the PTFL spectrum and codes 9690.

Paediatric nodal marginal zone lymphoma is now regarded as part of the paediatric-type follicular lymphoma spectrum — a pNMZL referral must NOT be auto-coded 9699 (Pathway §3.5). The follicular node applies that guard.

Mantle cell lymphoma. SOX11 supports a cyclin D1-negative case. Note the inverse trap: a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CCND1 rearrangement codes 9680, NOT 9673 (Pathway §5.2). In situ mantle cell neoplasia is an incidental lesion and is not registered.

B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukaemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma. This code is topography-restricted away from C42.0 blood, C42.1 marrow and C42.3 RES — a blood or marrow presentation resolves to Group I, not Group II. C42.2 spleen is re-admitted. Confirm the compartment before accepting the code.
Waldenström macroglobulinaemia — lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with an IgM paraprotein. Vanishingly rare in a paediatric registry: a populated 9761 warrants review before acceptance.
Malignant lymphoma, lymphoplasmacytic. Record the paraprotein if one is documented — an IgM paraprotein with marrow involvement is 9761.

Immunoproliferative small intestinal disease (alpha heavy chain disease). Record the heavy-chain result. If the report describes only a marginal-zone infiltrate without alpha heavy chain, code 9699 instead.

positive: Skin-limited lesion on head or trunk
resolution_logic.coding_note: Primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma — head or trunk, BCL2 usually negative or weak, indolent. Distinct from the cutaneous T-cell entities carried in the cutaneous tree. Confirm there is no nodal or systemic disease before accepting a primary cutaneous code.

positive: EBER positive in >80% of viable tumour cells
resolution_logic.coding_note: EBV-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS requires >80% of viable malignant cells EBER-positive. It has no separate ICD-O-3 code. Note the two nearby entities that also have none: EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer (solitary, sharply circumscribed, non-infiltrative, no lymphadenopathy, no organomegaly, no marrow involvement, blood EBV DNA not raised — ≥2 lesions disqualifies it; it regresses on reduction of immunosuppression, so coding it as aggressive lymphoma triggers unnecessary chemotherapy) and EBV-positive polymorphic B-cell LPD NOS.

Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder. Tissue biopsy with WHO classification is the gold standard — EBV DNA load is a screening and monitoring tool, not a diagnostic one, and cannot on its own reach 9971. A material proportion of PTLD is EBV-negative, so a negative EBER does not exclude it. Under ICD-O-3.2 polymorphic PTLD is 9971/1 and monomorphic PTLD codes to the specific lymphoma — code the specific entity where the morphology supports one. Where paediatric solid-organ transplantation is not performed, a populated 9971 warrants review before acceptance.
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, immunoblastic. Use only where the report explicitly describes immunoblastic morphology; otherwise 9680.

positive: Cytogenetics / FISH report is in the file
resolution_logic.coding_note: A large B-cell lymphoma with a FISH report available — resolve MYC, BCL2, BCL6, IRF4 and CCND1 before terminating.

positive: Localised head-and-neck or Waldeyer's-ring mass, stage I–II
resolution_logic.upgrade_path: IRF4 break-apart FISH would identify large B-cell lymphoma with IRF4 rearrangement, which NHL-BFM de-escalates. It is cryptic in about 10% of cases.

provisional_pending.reason: possible LBCL-IRF4
alternative_entities: Large B-cell lymphoma with IRF4 rearrangement

resolution_logic.coding_note: Malignant lymphoma, small B lymphocytic, NOS. Use only for a small-cell B lymphoid proliferation with no mantle, marginal-zone or follicular pattern and no CD5/CD10. If the pattern is marginal zone, code 9699; if follicular, use the follicular node.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 break-apart FISH would identify high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 (± BCL6) rearrangements, which has no ICD-O-3 code and is otherwise absorbed here.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma NOS — the landing code for HGBL-MYC/BCL2 (±BCL6), HGBL NOS, primary bone DLBCL, DLBCL with CCND1 rearrangement, fibrin-associated DLBCL, DLBCL with chronic inflammation and pyothorax-associated lymphoma, none of which has its own code (Pathway §5.2).

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: A full B-cell panel with CD10, BCL6, BCL2, Ki-67, MUM1 and CD138 would reach an entity-level code.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Immunoproliferative disease NOS. Use only where the report describes an immunoproliferative lesion that cannot be placed — prefer 9591 where the process is clearly lymphomatous.

nos_fallback.reason: Mature B lineage established but no entity-defining combination met. 9680 is the large-cell-context family label; where the cells are small and the pattern is not large-cell, use the 'uncertain subtype' escape rather than accepting this fallback.

nodes.hint: Four codes separated by three stains: HHV-8 LANA-1, ALK and CD138. Each of the three is a hard gate — without the stain the code is unassignable, not merely uncertain.
nodes.coding_note: Hard rules (Pathway §3.4): 9678 and 9738 CANNOT be assigned without LANA-1; 9737 CANNOT be assigned without ALK IHC. nodes.question: Which cytogenetic or FISH finding does the report give? Pick the row that also matches the morphology that brought this case here.
nodes.hint: Sequential algorithm where only one test is affordable: MYC break-apart FIRST (accept a 5–10% miss rate), then BCL2 and BCL6 only if MYC is rearranged; if MYC is negative and the morphology fits Burkitt, test 11q. Run it on the FNA cell block — failure is about 1%.
nodes.coding_note: Four of the six FISH-defined entities in this group have no ICD-O-3 code, so their unavailability costs nothing at code level — but two of them are Burkitt mimics and their absence causes silent misclassification into 9687. This node exists to make that visible (Pathway §4.2).

options.finding: MYC break-apart POSITIVE — Burkitt morphology and phenotype (CD20+, BCL2−, Ki-67 ≥90%, TdT−)
options.coding_note: Burkitt lymphoma with IG::MYC demonstrated — the essential criterion in WHO-HAEM5. WHO-HAEM5 splits Burkitt into EBV-positive and EBV-negative; ICC does not adopt the split and neither has an ICD-O code, so record eber_status regardless.

options.finding: MYC break-apart NEGATIVE — but 11q23.2–23.3 gain WITH telomeric loss at 11q24.1-qter is demonstrated, Burkitt-like morphology with coarse apoptotic bodies
options.coding_note: High-grade/large B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration has NO ICD-O-3 code and falls back to 9687 with a named flag rather than being absorbed silently. Gain alone is non-specific and insufficient — the telomeric loss is required. MYC expression is weak (20–60%) and LMO2 (SP51) is positive in 46%, against Burkitt's LMO2-negativity.

options.finding: MYC break-apart NEGATIVE, 11q NOT tested — Burkitt morphology and phenotype
options.upgrade_path: 11q gain/loss FISH would identify high-grade/large B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration, which has no code and is otherwise absorbed here — the highest-volume error in this group.
options.coding_note: Absence of MYC does not exclude Burkitt: Ogwang's own definition allows 'c-MYC positive OR no c-MYC signal by FISH', and some morphologically and phenotypically typical cases show no MYC rearrangement (Gerhard-Hartmann). The fallback is not 'not Burkitt' — it is 9687 with the flag.

provisional_pending.reason: MYC break-apart negative and 11q not tested; HG/LBCL-11q not excluded.

options.finding: MYC rearranged PLUS BCL2 rearranged (± BCL6) — large-cell or high-grade morphology
options.coding_note: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 (± BCL6) rearrangements has NO ICD-O-3 code and is absorbed into 9680 (Pathway §5.2). Record the fusion partners as free text so the case is recoverable when a code exists.

options.finding: MYC and BCL6 rearranged, BCL2 germline
options.coding_note: WHO-HAEM5 calls this DLBCL-NOS or HGBL-NOS; ICC retains a provisional HGBCL-MYC/BCL6 category. Both resolve to 9680 (Pathway §5.3). Map the ICC provisional to a medium-confidence flag.

options.finding: IRF4 rearranged — localised head-and-neck or Waldeyer's-ring mass in a child
options.coding_note: Large B-cell lymphoma with IRF4 rearrangement has NO ICD-O-3 code and falls to 9680 with the flag. Absorbing it into 9698 instead drives over-treatment of a curable paediatric head-and-neck disease. Cryptic in about 10%, so a negative IRF4 FISH does not fully exclude it.

options.finding: t(14;18) BCL2 rearranged with a follicular architecture
options.coding_note: BCL2 rearrangement establishes an adult-pattern follicular lymphoma and excludes paediatric-type follicular lymphoma. Return to the follicular node for the grade.

options.finding: CCND1 / t(11;14) rearranged with mantle-cell morphology and cyclin D1 positive
CCND1 rearranged in a DIFFUSE LARGE B-CELL lymphoma — not mantle-cell morphology
options.coding_note: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CCND1 rearrangement codes 9680, NOT 9673 (Pathway §5.2). The rearrangement does not make it mantle cell lymphoma.

options.finding: IG::MYC with i(1)(q10) or tetrasomy 1q, in a CD20-negative, sIg-negative, CD19+/PAX5+/CD10+/MUM1+ tumour
FISH panel negative for BCL2-R, BCL6-R, MYC-R and IRF4-R in a follicular lesion
options.coding_note: This is the FISH profile of paediatric-type follicular lymphoma. Return to the follicular node, which applies the do-not-grade rule.

options.finding: FISH was attempted and FAILED — hybridisation failure, necrotic or over-fixed material
options.upgrade_path: Repeat FISH on better-fixed material. Buffered formalin under 72 hours is the standard (Emile 2016); with prolonged or unbuffered fixation MYC FISH nuclear signal falls to 3%. On an adequately fixed cell block the failure rate is only about 1%.
options.coding_note: Attempted-and-failed is NOT the same as not-done and must not be recorded as an excluded rearrangement. Where the entering morphology was Burkitt, use the Burkitt terminal at the mature B node instead, which carries the correct provisional.

options.finding: FISH is not available at this facility
options.upgrade_path: MYC, BCL2, BCL6, 11q and IRF4 FISH are unavailable at this facility, so the FISH-defined entities cannot be separated here. Plasma ctDNA gives a Burkitt versus non-Burkitt binary with turnaround 6.5 days against 46.8 days for tissue, where an 8 mL ccfDNA tube can reach a laboratory within 72 hours.
options.coding_note: A permanent unavailable-workup terminal, recorded as such rather than passed off as a completed workup.

nos_fallback.reason: FISH performed but no listed rearrangement was found. The code that entered this node stands where one was set; 9680 is the large-B-cell default and must not be accepted for a case that entered with Burkitt morphology — use the Burkitt terminal, which carries the MYC provisional.

nodes.hint: Two rules are tested before everything else because they change the answer most often: two or more TFH markers move a case OUT of 9702 into 9705, and a positive HTLV-1 serology makes it 9827. Both are cheap.
nodes.coding_note: CD3 is absent in more than 75% of ALCL — CD3-negativity does not exclude a T-cell lymphoma, and a 'null cell' phenotype is marker loss, not a separate code. cCD3+/sCD3− is a flow phenotype and IHC usually cannot make the distinction, so an IHC-only tier cannot fully resolve T lineage. TCR clonality must never be used for lineage assignment.

resolution_logic.coding_note: THE RE-ROUTING RULE: 'PTCL expressing 2 or more TFH markers should be classified as nodal TFH lymphoma, NOS' (Miranda 2024). A case that would otherwise fall to 9702 moves to 9705 on two markers. Because 9702 is this branch's default, this is the single highest-volume correction in IIb3 — and it must be tested BEFORE any unconditioned 9702 rule or it never fires (Pathway §3.7).

Adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma. HTLV-1 serology is the absolute gate — without it the code is unassignable. Shimoyama subtyping needs blood counts, LDH, calcium, skin examination and nodal status together; the pathology report cannot subtype, and the Shimoyama numeric criteria are not in this pathway's source set. This code is topography-restricted away from C42.0, C42.1 and C42.3 — confirm the compartment. In HTLV-1 low-prevalence regions it should be near-empty and a populated 9827 warrants review.

positive: Leukaemic NK-cell picture with rapid deterioration
resolution_logic.reason: Aggressive NK-cell leukaemia is a separate entity with no code in this group and is a haemophagocytic emergency, rapidly fatal. It is not extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma and must not be coded 9719. Route it to Group I and record it as a named uncoded entity.

resolution_logic.coding_note: ALK is IHC, not FISH — the single highest-yield rule in this group. Under ICD-O-3.2 9714 is 'ALCL, ALK-positive'; its Layer 1 name, 'Anaplastic large cell lymphoma, T cell and Null cell type', is the pre-split ICD-O-3.1 term and is NOT edited here. A cutaneous CD30-positive lesion that is ALK-positive or t(2;5)-positive is NOT primary cutaneous — it is secondary involvement by systemic ALCL and codes 9714. Rigaud's minimum staging survives the no-PET reality: biopsy of sufficient size, blood minimal disseminated disease, marrow aspirate, lumbar puncture, chest X-ray and abdominal and cervical ultrasound.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None outstanding for the code itself. DUSP22 rearrangement (45% of ALK-negative cases) and TP63 rearrangement (2%) refine the prognosis and have no ICD-O code — record them as variables. 9715 has no Group 2 REDCap option yet, so the clerk cannot select it until the registrar adds it; the case is complete either way.
resolution_logic.coding_note: ALK-negative systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma. Coded 9715 from 4 Sep 2026 (registrar ruling 2). Until then the case rode on 9714, whose ICD-O-3.1 name spans both. 9715 has no Group 2 REDCap option and no ICCC-2017 range yet — both on the to-do list. In a child this result is a re-review trigger: >95% of paediatric ALCL is ALK-positive.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: ALK immunohistochemistry (clone ALK-1) is ONE antibody and separates 9714 from ALK-negative ALCL and both from the primary cutaneous CD30+ entity. It also detects ALK-positive histiocytosis at no additional cost.
resolution_logic.coding_note: CD30-positive with ALK not done is 9702 — the upgrade path is one antibody (Pathway §3.6). Do not emit 9714 without a documented ALK result: that is a viral-or-marker-gated code emitted without the gating result.

positive: Hepatosplenomegaly with liver failure shortly after primary EBV infection, in an immunocompetent child
resolution_logic.coding_note: Systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disease of childhood: an IMMUNOCOMPETENT patient with hepatosplenomegaly and liver failure, ± lymphadenopathy, rash, coagulopathy, HLH and multiorgan failure, shortly after primary EBV infection or complicating systemic chronic active EBV disease. Biopsy shows lymphoid infiltration with usually minimal nuclear atypia, T-lineage markers and EBER; phenotype CD2, CD3, TIA-1, CD8 in acute and CD4 in chronic. Because the histology is non-specific, clinical correlation is essential — 9724 is a code a pathology report can never establish alone. Neither retained source mentions Africa for any T/NK entity, so outside Asia and Latin America a populated 9724 warrants review rather than acceptance.

positive: Hepatosplenomegaly with liver failure shortly after primary EBV infection, in an immunocompetent child
resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Repeat EBER ISH with a passing control probe (U6). The control failed, so the EBV status is unknown — it is NOT negative, and 9724 is hard-gated on a positive EBER.
resolution_logic.coding_note: An EBER negative without a passing control is 'not assessable', never negative (Pathway §4.3, §7.3 item 4). This branch is deliberately separate from the not-done branch and from any negative branch.
Routed to the cutaneous tree, which carries hydroa vacciniforme-like disease and its behaviour split. Tested before the 9708 rule deliberately.

Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma: αβ lineage (βF1 POSITIVE), CD4−/CD8+, CD56 NEGATIVE, cytotoxic proteins positive, EBV negative. CD56 is not in the SPTCL phenotype at all, which makes it a clean discriminator. A subset of REACTIVE T cells in SPTCL expresses TCR γ/δ — a γδ-positive population is therefore not sufficient for the gamma-delta entity; the γδ cells must be the neoplastic ones. Germline HAVCR2 mutations occur in 25% (up to 85% in Asian populations) — a variable to capture, not a criterion.

The primary cutaneous gamma-delta entity (9726) is carried in the cutaneous tree, where the MF/LyP anti-miscoding rule and the Vδ1 / Vδ2 split are applied. Vδ2 involves subcutaneous tissue, ulcerates more and is precisely the form that will be mistaken for 9708.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: βF1 and CD56 are the minimum panel — without them a lobular panniculitic infiltrate cannot be coded beyond 9702. The two entities they separate have 5-year disease-specific survivals of 87% and 11%.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Neither βF1 nor CD56 was recorded, so neither 9708 nor the gamma-delta entity may be emitted.

positive: Hepatosplenic disease without lymphadenopathy, marrow sinusoidal infiltrate
resolution_logic.coding_note: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma. Marrow involvement is virtually constant and the pattern is the finding: CD3 highlights neoplastic lymphocytes distending the sinuses — highly characteristic. Phenotype CD2, CD3, CD7; TCR-delta 75% / TCR-beta 20% / TCR-silent 5%; CD56 positive; CD8 in only 20%; TIA-1 95%; perforin and granzyme B 40%. Cytogenetics i(7q), trisomy 8. Presentation is usually stage IV.

Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma. Where coeliac disease is uncommon an intestinal T-cell lymphoma is far more likely MEITL than EATL — but ICD-O-3 gives ONE code for both, so the distinction is a captured variable, not a branch. Record intestinal_tcl_subtype = MEITL. Phenotype CD8+ (most), CD56+ (most), TCR-delta ~50% / beta ~35%, nuclear MATK, cytoplasmic SYK, CD20 in ~20%; genetics SETD2 ~90%, JAK-STAT 80–90%.

Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma — near-constant coeliac association, HLA-DQ2/DQ8, Caucasians and Northern Europe. Large pleomorphic cells with eosinophils and histiocytes; CD3, CD7; CD2 variably negative, CD5 often negative; CD8 in ~25%, usually CD8− and CD56−; TCRαβ; CD30 in a subset; CD103. Record intestinal_tcl_subtype = EATL. Miranda does not state which entity 9717 maps to — the registry codes both here and records the subtype.

Intestinal T-cell lymphoma, NOS — the subtype could not be separated. Record intestinal_tcl_subtype = NOS. Check the indolent NK-cell lesion of the GI tract first: it is CD56+, sCD3−, cytotoxic+ and EBV-NEGATIVE, and it is a non-reportable exit, not a lymphoma.

positive: Nodal disease only, no nasal involvement
resolution_logic.coding_note: EBV-positive nodal T- and NK-cell lymphoma is newly listed in WHO-HAEM5 and has no code. It is NOT the nodal counterpart of 9719 and must not be coded as one — the NK/T node applies the distinguishing features and terminates it at 9702.
T-gamma lymphoproliferative disease — the ICD-O-3 term for T-cell large granular lymphocytic proliferation. Confirm the compartment: a purely blood and marrow presentation resolves to Group I.

Mycosis fungoides, Sézary syndrome, the primary cutaneous CD30+ behaviour split, the 9709 entity boundary and primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma NOS are all resolved in the cutaneous tree. Note that 9709 is NOT the fallback for primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma NOS — that is 9702 with site = skin (Pathway §5.2).

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: 9705 requires TWO or more TFH markers. The five-marker working panel is CD10, PD-1/CD279, ICOS, CXCL13 and BCL6; PD-1 and BCL6 are already stocked for the cutaneous panel, so the marginal cost is CD10 plus CXCL13 or ICOS.
resolution_logic.coding_note: One marker is not enough. Do not emit 9705 on a single TFH marker.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: ALK immunostaining, HTLV-1 serology, EBER ISH and a two-marker TFH panel are each cheap and each can change the code. Record which were done.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Mature T-cell lymphoma NOS — also the declared fallback for primary nodal EBV-positive T/NK lymphoma, primary cutaneous acral CD8+ T-cell lymphoma, indolent T-cell lymphoma of the GI tract and primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma NOS, none of which has a code (Pathway §5.2).

nodes.question: A cytotoxic CD56-positive or nasal-type lesion. What does the EBER in-situ hybridisation show?
nodes.hint: This is the one node in the group where a NEGATIVE EBER changes the answer rather than lowering the ceiling. Read the control probe result before reading the EBER result.
nodes.coding_note: EBER ISH on tissue is the only entity-defining EBV test. LMP1 is absent in latency I and 0 and is explicitly forbidden in plasmablastic lymphoma. Serology cannot upgrade any code — VCA IgG+/IgM−/EBNA-1 IgG+ is the near-universal state in a high-EBV-burden population, EBNA-1 IgG is unreliable in HIV-positive patients, and the heterophile test has a high false-negative rate in young children. Viral load has no agreed threshold, unit or specimen and cannot be compared between laboratories (Pathway §4.3).

prior_probability.context: extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type, and chronic active EBV disease
prior_probability.interpretation: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma is consistently EBER-positive — expected positivity is 100%, which is why a genuine EBER-negative result here changes the entity rather than lowering the ceiling. That makes the control-failure distinction carry more weight at this node than anywhere else in the tree: an uninterpretable EBER must not be read as the negative that would exclude 9719.

resolution_logic.reason: Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract — small, well-circumscribed, superficial lesions with only moderate atypia, CD56 and cytotoxic markers positive, surface CD3 negative, and EBV NEGATIVE on a test with a passing control. EBV-negativity is what stops this being over-called as 9719, which is consistently EBER-positive. Often persistent with minimal potential to disseminate. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. Record it as a named uncoded entity; a subset carries JAK3 mutations, and WHO-HAEM5 has renamed it indolent T-cell lymphoma of the GI tract, which will need a code decision.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Repeat EBER ISH with a passing control probe (U6). The control failed, so the EBV status is UNKNOWN. It is not negative, and only a genuine negative with a passing control can support the indolent non-reportable exit.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Deliberately routed away from the non-reportable branch. Emitting the indolent exit here would drop a possible 9719 from the registry on a test that never ran; emitting 9719 would claim an EBV result that does not exist. 9702 with the repeat named is the only honest terminal.

provisional_pending.reason: EBER is **not assessable** here, and at this node that matters more than anywhere else in the group: a *negative* EBER with a passing control is what separates indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract — a non-reportable lesion — from 9719, which is consistently EBER-positive. A failed control cannot make that call. Repeat EBER on a fresh section before accepting either answer.
alternative_entities: Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract — non-reportable

resolution_logic.coding_note: CD2+, surface CD3 negative but cytoplasmic CD3ε positive, CD56+, cytotoxic (granzyme B / TIA-1 / perforin)+, EBER POSITIVE. T-lineage origin (10–40% of cases) does not change the code. WHO-HAEM5 drops the 'nasal type' qualifier — alias it, do not edit the name.
Non-nasal presentations require exclusion of an occult nasal primary. Record pet_ct_available and whether blind nasal biopsies were done.

positive: Nodal disease only, no nasal involvement
