It is NOT the nodal counterpart of 9719 and must not be coded as one. Distinguishing features: no nasal involvement, median age 61–64 against 48 for ENKTL, CD56 usually negative, T-lineage far commoner than NK (<20% NK) — the reverse of ENKTL — coagulative necrosis and angioinvasion uncommon, and prognosis worse. Diagnosis mandates exclusion of underlying immunodeficiency, of ENKTL and of systemic EBV-positive lymphoproliferative disease of childhood.

positive: Leukaemic NK-cell picture with rapid deterioration
resolution_logic.reason: Aggressive NK-cell leukaemia is a haemophagocytic emergency and is rapidly fatal. It has no code in this group, is a separate entity from extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, and must not be coded 9719. Route to Group I and record it as a named uncoded entity.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None for 9719 — a genuine EBER-negative result with a passing control excludes it. Consider the EBV-negative differential: indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the GI tract at a gastrointestinal site, or a cytotoxic peripheral T-cell lymphoma elsewhere.
resolution_logic.coding_note: EBER negative with a passing control. 9719 requires EBER positivity — 'demonstration of EBV infection is a requisite'. Without it the ceiling is 9702, and this branch may not emit 9719.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Repeat EBER ISH with a passing control probe (U6). The control failed, so the result is uninterpretable — record it as 'not assessable', never as negative. Check the fixation: buffered formalin under 72 hours is the standard, and EBER survives fixation better than most markers, so a control failure often means the block is badly compromised for every other stain too.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Deliberately separated from the EBER-negative branch. The negative branch closes the 9719 question; this one leaves it open, and the difference must be visible on the record.

provisional_pending.reason: EBER was performed but is **not assessable** — the RNA control probe (U6) failed, or the section was uninterpretable. This is not a negative result: 3 of 21 cases in the Kenyan series were uninterpretable on exactly this basis. 9719 requires demonstrated EBV infection, so the case cannot be closed either way until EBER is repeated on a fresh section.
alternative_entities: Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract — non-reportable

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: EBER in-situ hybridisation with a control probe (U6) has not been performed. It is a hard prerequisite for 9719, 9724 and 9725 and nothing substitutes for it — LMP1 is absent in latency I and 0. Order it.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Not done is distinct from not assessable: here the test can still be ordered on the existing block.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: EBER ISH with a control probe is the entity-defining test for 9719.

nodes.question: A blastic lymphoid population. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: B-lineage needs TdT plus CD34, or bright CD10 with low CD45, low or absent CD20 and absent surface Ig. T-lineage needs TdT plus CD1a, or CD34 — CD34 is positive in only about a third of T-LBL, so CD34-negative does not exclude.
nodes.coding_note: 9728 and 9729 are retired in ICD-O-3.2 and are NOT emitted by this tool — every route that would have reached them reaches 9811 or 9837. After that change the Group I / Group II split for lymphoblastic disease is carried ENTIRELY by topography, so the compartment gate result must be on the record. TdT negative by flow does not exclude T-LBL: it was flow-negative in 7 of 15 cases and positive by cell-block immunocytochemistry in all seven — always reflex to cell-block ICC (Bhaker 2015).

Record the MPO percentage AND the method: proposals range from 3% to 28%, >10% improves specificity, and no consensus threshold exists, so the number and the method must both be on the record. WHO-HAEM5 gives no per-lineage blast threshold; ICC proposes >5%.

No lineage-defining marker was found — acute undifferentiated leukaemia or acute leukaemia of ambiguous lineage, neither of which has a Group II code. Code from the Group I acute-leukaemia tree, which carries the panel-adequacy rules.

This is a tumour-like lesion, not a lymphoblastic lymphoma, and must not be coded 9727 or 9837. It is a hard false-positive guard (Pathway §3.2). Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Tested before every B-lineage rule below. The registry follows ICC here because it reverses the 2016 WHO rule and is the actionable one (Pathway §5.3).

resolution_logic.coding_note: ETP requires cCD3+ AND CD1a <5% AND CD8 <5% AND CD5 absent-or-dim (<75% of blasts) AND ≥1 of CD11b/CD13/CD33/CD65/CD117 or CD34/HLA-DR at ≥25% AND MPO <3%. It has no separate code — still 9837. MPO is the discriminator against T/myeloid mixed-phenotype disease: that is MPO-positive on the Bras threshold, ETP is MPO-negative.

T-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma. 9729 is retired in ICD-O-3.2 and this tool does not emit it. This code is topography-restricted away from C42.0 blood, C42.1 marrow and C42.3 RES — a marrow-dominant case resolves to Group I. Confirm the compartment-gate result before accepting the code.
cCD3 with TdT establishes T-lineage lymphoblastic disease. CD1a or CD34 strengthens the immaturity call but CD34 is positive in only about a third of T-LBL.

nodes.question: Which cytogenetic, FISH or ploidy finding does the report give?
nodes.hint: Where FISH is scarce, the stated priority is a triple panel — ETV6::RUNX1 fusion, BCR::ABL1 fusion and KMT2A break-apart — plus DNA ploidy by flow or FISH, which is explicitly named as cheap and available.
nodes.coding_note: These codes are topography-restricted away from C42.0 blood, C42.1 marrow and C42.3 RES; C42.2 spleen is re-admitted. Confirm the compartment-gate result before accepting any of them — a marrow-dominant case belongs to Group I. BCR::ABL1 is 'paramount' because it is TKI-actionable.

options.finding: t(12;21)(p13;q22) ETV6::RUNX1 (TEL-AML1)
options.coding_note: Cryptic — never visible on karyotype. Only FISH or RT-PCR can establish or exclude it, so a normal karyotype closes nothing.
Record the p190 versus p210 isoform. Paramount because it is TKI-actionable.

options.finding: t(v;11q23) KMT2A (MLL) rearranged
options.coding_note: KMT2A break-apart FISH is the required method. The phenotype is CD10-dim or negative with weak cCD22/cCD79a and can drop out of the lineage scheme — it must not default to a myeloid or mixed-phenotype code.

options.finding: Hyperdiploidy — modal number above 50 chromosomes, or DNA index consistent with high hyperdiploidy
Hypodiploidy — low hypodiploid 32–39 chromosomes, or near-haploid 24–31

options.coding_note: Clinical clue: eosinophilia. Confirm with FISH.
Phenotype clue: CD9 strong, CD34 negative.

options.finding: BCR::ABL1-like (Ph-like) signature — CRLF2-r, ABL-class or JAK-class kinase fusion, with BCR::ABL1 and ETV6::RUNX1 already excluded
options.coding_note: Prior exclusion of BCR::ABL1 and ETV6::RUNX1 is a hard prerequisite. The seven-probe break-apart panel (CRLF2, ABL1, ABL2, JAK2, PDGFRB, CSF1R, EPOR) captures only 69.7–73.2%, and flow CRLF2 is a screening entry point only — about 92% sensitive for a CRLF2 rearrangement, but CRLF2-r occurs in only about half of Ph-like cases. Resolved at the molecular node.

options.finding: An uncoded B-lymphoblastic subtype — iAMP21, DUX4-r, ZNF384-r, MEF2D-r, NUTM1-r, PAX5 P80R or another entity with no ICD-O-3 code
options.coding_note: No ICD-O-3 code exists for these. They fall back to 9811 with the genotype recorded, or the information is lost permanently (Pathway §5.2).

options.finding: T-lineage disease — no ICD-O-3 code changes on the genetic result
options.upgrade_path: None at code level — T-lymphoblastic genetics, including the early T-cell precursor phenotype, do not change the ICD-O-3 code. Record the genotype on the case.
options.coding_note: 9829 does not exist in this group's list and 9729 is retired: T-lineage lymphoblastic disease codes 9837 regardless of genetics.

options.finding: Karyotype normal AND the cryptic panel (ETV6::RUNX1 by FISH or RT-PCR, plus ploidy by DNA index or SNP array) was NEGATIVE
options.upgrade_path: None — the cryptic set has been excluded by an adequate method.
options.coding_note: The cryptic branch has been properly closed. 9811 is a defensible terminal here, not an incomplete workup.

options.finding: Karyotype normal — FISH and RT-PCR NOT performed
options.upgrade_path: A normal karyotype does not exclude ETV6::RUNX1 (cryptic, needs FISH or RT-PCR) or masked hypodiploidy (needs SNP array or DNA index). Both remain open.
options.coding_note: Recorded as an open cryptic branch, not as an excluded one. Do not declare the cytogenetic workup complete here.

options.finding: FISH attempted and FAILED, or cytogenetics not available at this facility
options.upgrade_path: The affordable triple panel — ETV6::RUNX1, BCR::ABL1, KMT2A break-apart — plus DNA ploidy by flow or FISH would upgrade this to 9812–9818. Recorded as unavailable, which is a legitimate permanent terminal state, not a completed workup.
options.coding_note: Attempted-and-failed and never-attempted are both recorded here but must be distinguished in fish_status. Neither is an excluded rearrangement.

nos_fallback.name: B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: B-lymphoblastic lineage established and no defining fusion or ploidy abnormality identified. T-lineage cases resolve at 9837 on their own option and must not fall through to this fallback.

nodes.question: Record the fusion, signature or mutation exactly as the report states it, and say whether a BCR-ABL1-like (Ph-like) signature was demonstrated.
nodes.capture_label: Genotype as reported (e.g. "CRLF2 rearrangement by FISH, BCR::ABL1 and ETV6::RUNX1 negative", "iAMP21 by FISH, 6 RUNX1 signals")
nodes.hint: The Ph-like signature is what separates 9819 from 9811. It needs a CRLF2 rearrangement, an ABL-class fusion or a JAK-STAT lesion by FISH or RNA-seq, with BCR::ABL1 itself negative. Where the test was not done or could not be read, the case stays at 9811 — the nearest code the evidence supports — and the missing test is named on the answer.
nodes.coding_note: 9819 (B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, BCR-ABL1-like) is built here from 4 Sep 2026 under registrar ruling 4 — one code, two groups, with the genetic layer beneath 9811. It needs a GEX/LDA signature, the seven-probe FISH panel or RNA-seq, so it is unreachable below full NGS capability; where the test was not done or could not be read the case stays at 9811, the nearest code the evidence supports, and the outstanding test is named on the answer (ruling 11). Built 4 Sep 2026 under registrar rulings 1-3: paediatric occurrence decides whether a code exists in the tree, and a code the REDCap option list lacks is reported and put on docs/codes-awaiting-redcap.md rather than withheld. The output block says the option is missing so the clerk knows to expect it.

resolution_logic.coding_note: BCR-ABL1-like (Ph-like) B-lymphoblastic lymphoma. Registrar ruling 4 of 4 Sep 2026: 9811 is carried in both groups and the genetic layer sits beneath it, so a nodal Ph-like case resolves here rather than terminating at NOS. About 15% of childhood ALL. No Group 2 REDCap option and no ICCC-2017 IIb1 range entry yet — both on the to-do list.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: A Ph-like signature — CRLF2 rearrangement, ABL-class fusion or JAK-STAT lesion by FISH or RNA-seq — would move this case to 9819. The genotype text is preserved meanwhile.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Ruling 11: an unperformed or unreadable signature test drops the case to the nearest code rather than dead-ending. 9811 is that code, with the outstanding test named.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None outstanding — the Ph-like signature was tested and is negative.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Screening was attempted and returned negative. Do not record this as "no abnormality sought".

nos_fallback.name: B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Uncoded B-lymphoblastic subtype — genotype preserved as a free-text annotation on 9811.

nodes.question: What is in this patient's file for the skin lesion? Pick the highest tier available, or the special context that applies.
nodes.hint: Cutaneous lymphoid disease is diagnosed clinically and pathologically together. The biopsy alone settles almost nothing here: three of the six codes in this branch turn on the clinical history, and one of them cannot be settled until follow-up. Read the clinic letters as well as the pathology report.
nodes.coding_note: This tree owns 9700, 9701, 9709/1, 9718 (/1 and /3), 9725 (/1 and /3) and 9726, and it is the only place the betaF1 / CD56 discrimination between 9708 and 9726 is taken. Reached from the main tree's lineage node by next_node g2cut_document_inventory, and directly from presentation_router.json for a skin presentation. Cross-tree next_node targets used by this tree: g2_document_inventory, g2_matureB, g2_matureT, g2hist_document_inventory, g2mast_document_inventory. Transferability (Pathway 3.7): neither retained source mentions Africa for any T/NK entity. Expect 9724 and 9725 to be near-empty in this catchment; a populated one warrants review rather than acceptance.

options.label: Referral, clinic or dermatology letter only — no skin biopsy in the file
Skin biopsy with H&E only — no immunohistochemistry
Skin biopsy with immunohistochemistry (with or without EBER in-situ hybridisation)
Skin biopsy with immunohistochemistry, plus TCR clonality, FISH, or blood flow cytometry
The skin lesion is one site of an established systemic or nodal lymphoma, or nodal / visceral disease dominates the picture
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover. A skin deposit of a systemic lymphoma is not a primary cutaneous entity and none of this tree's codes apply to it. The main lymphoid tree owns the nodal and extranodal presentations.

options.label: The infiltrate is B-lineage — CD20, CD79a or PAX5 positive and CD3 negative
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover. The primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas, including primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma (9597), are owned by the main tree's mature B-cell branch. This tree covers the T-cell and NK-cell cutaneous entities only.

options.label: The infiltrate is Langerhans cell or histiocytic — CD1a, CD207 / langerin, S100, CD68 or CD163 positive
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover to the histiocytic and dendritic tree. Langerhans cell histiocytosis very often presents in skin and must not be worked up as a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

options.label: The infiltrate is mast cell — tryptase or CD117 positive, or the report says urticaria pigmentosa or mastocytoma
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover to the mast cell tree.

options.label: The file establishes a non-neoplastic skin condition — infection, drug reaction, pseudolymphoma or another mimic
Malignancy excluded on review — the diagnosis was revised and no lymphoid neoplasm is present
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinic letter say?
nodes.hint: A letter naming an entity is not a biopsy. At this tier the wording chooses a placeholder code, never the entity itself — and two of the wordings below name conditions that are not cancers at all.
nodes.coding_note: Referral-only tier: confidence is LOW throughout and every downstream test is listed as an upgrade. 9590 is the honest placeholder for a suspected cutaneous lymphoma with no tissue. Never record a /1 behaviour from a letter — 9718/1 and 9725/1 leave ICCC-3 Group II, and doing that on a letter would delete a case that a biopsy may show to be reportable.

options.label: Letter reads "mycosis fungoides", "cutaneous T-cell lymphoma" or "CTCL" — no biopsy in the file
options.upgrade_path: A skin biopsy with CD2, CD3, CD4, CD5, CD7, CD8 and betaF1, read together with the clinical description of the patches and plaques, would resolve 9700.
options.coding_note: Mycosis fungoides is a clinicopathological diagnosis. The word in a letter supports neither the epidermotropic infiltrate nor the clinical course. In children the hypopigmented mimics — pityriasis lichenoides, post-inflammatory hypopigmentation, atopic dermatitis — are far commoner than the disease.

options.label: Letter reads "Sezary syndrome", or "erythroderma with circulating Sezary cells" — no blood or biopsy report
options.upgrade_path: Blood flow cytometry (CD4/CD8 ratio, CD4+CD7−, CD4+CD26−, KIR3DL2), a Sezary cell count on the smear, and TCR clonality showing an identical clone in blood and skin, would resolve 9701.
options.coding_note: 9701 requires an identical T-cell clone in blood and skin plus one of the blood criteria. None of that is in a letter.

options.label: Letter reads "lymphomatoid papulosis", or describes recurrent crops of self-healing papules — no biopsy in the file
options.upgrade_path: A skin biopsy with CD30 and ALK immunohistochemistry, plus staging for extracutaneous disease, would resolve 9718 (either behaviour) or 9714.
options.coding_note: Do NOT record 9718/1 from a letter. Lymphomatoid papulosis is /1 and leaves Group II; primary cutaneous ALCL is /3 and stays. Only the biopsy, ALK and staging can tell them apart, and 9590 keeps the case in the registry until they do.

options.label: Letter reads "primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma", "cutaneous ALCL" or "CD30-positive skin lymphoma" — no biopsy in the file
options.upgrade_path: A skin biopsy with CD30 and ALK immunohistochemistry, plus staging, would resolve 9718/3 or 9714.

options.label: Letter reads "cutaneous lymphoma" or "skin lymphoma", type not stated; or "skin nodule, query lymphoma"
options.upgrade_path: A skin biopsy with a lineage panel (CD3, CD20, CD30, CD56) would open the T-cell, B-cell or histiocytic branch.
options.coding_note: Lineage is not stated, so 9702 would assert a T-cell origin the letter does not support. 9590 is the honest placeholder and keeps a suspected lymphoma on the registry.

options.label: Letter reads "hydroa vacciniforme", "photodermatosis" or "severe reaction to mosquito bites" — no biopsy in the file
options.reason: Classic hydroa vacciniforme is a photodermatosis and severe mosquito-bite allergy is a hypersensitivity reaction — neither is a neoplasm. They are separated from hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder only by an EBER-positive atypical T-cell or NK-cell infiltrate on a skin biopsy, and a letter cannot show that. No code is emitted. Re-enter this case as soon as a skin biopsy with EBER in-situ hybridisation is available, and immediately if the child develops fever, lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.

options.label: Letter reads "panniculitis", "cytophagic histiocytic panniculitis" or "erythema nodosum" — no biopsy in the file
options.reason: A clinical diagnosis of panniculitis names an inflammatory condition, not a neoplasm, and no code is emitted. Re-enter this case if a biopsy is taken: a lobular panniculitic infiltrate needs betaF1 and CD56 before it can be coded at all, and the two entities it may turn out to be have five-year survivals of 87% and 11%.

options.label: The letter names no diagnosis at all
options.upgrade_path: A skin biopsy is the first requirement. Nothing in this branch is codeable without one.

nodes.question: What does the skin biopsy report describe on H&E?
nodes.hint: Immunohistochemistry has not been done. No cutaneous T-cell entity in this branch is diagnosable on H&E alone — every option here is a placeholder with a named upgrade.
nodes.coding_note: Morphology-only tier: 9591 where a lymphoid malignancy is established but lineage is not, 9590 where even that is uncertain. 9702 is deliberately unreachable at this tier because it asserts a mature T-cell lineage that only immunohistochemistry can establish.

options.label: Band-like epidermotropic infiltrate of small cerebriform lymphocytes with Pautrier microabscesses, in long-standing patches or plaques
options.upgrade_path: CD2, CD3, CD4, CD5, CD7, CD8 and betaF1, read together with the clinical description, would resolve 9700.
options.coding_note: The H&E picture is characteristic but mycosis fungoides is a clinicopathological diagnosis and the phenotype is part of it. 9591 keeps the case on the registry without asserting the entity.

options.label: Dermal sheets of large anaplastic cells with horseshoe nuclei, in a solitary or grouped nodule
options.upgrade_path: CD30, ALK, EMA and a T-cell panel, plus staging for extracutaneous disease, would resolve 9718/3 or 9714.

options.label: Wedge-shaped mixed dermal infiltrate with large atypical cells and necrosis, in recurrent crops of lesions that crust and heal
options.upgrade_path: CD30 with an estimate of the positive fraction, ALK immunohistochemistry, and staging for extracutaneous disease, would resolve 9718 (either behaviour) or 9714.
options.coding_note: Lymphomatoid papulosis type C is histologically identical to primary cutaneous ALCL and the consensus concedes the distinction can be impossible on the section. Do not record a /1 behaviour at this tier — that would remove a possibly reportable cancer from the registry on an incomplete workup.

options.label: Lobular panniculitis with atypical lymphocytes rimming individual adipocytes
options.upgrade_path: betaF1, CD56, CD4, CD8, a cytotoxic panel (TIA-1, granzyme B, perforin) and EBER in-situ hybridisation would resolve 9708 or 9726. Without betaF1 and CD56 a lobular panniculitic infiltrate cannot be coded beyond 9702.
options.coding_note: In a child, an EBER-positive panniculitic lesion is more likely to belong to the cutaneous chronic active EBV family (9725) than to be 9708 — an NK-phenotype hydroa vacciniforme-like LPD mimics it. Order EBER alongside betaF1 and CD56.

options.label: Dense nodular-to-diffuse dermal infiltrate of small-to-medium pleomorphic lymphocytes, in a solitary plaque or tumour
options.upgrade_path: CD3, CD4, CD8, PD-1/CD279, BCL6, CXCL13 and Ki-67, with an estimate of the large pleomorphic cell fraction, would resolve 9709/1 or 9702/3.

options.label: Papulovesicular, necrotic or ulcerating lesions on sun-exposed skin, with a dermal lymphoid infiltrate

provisional_pending.reason: EBER in-situ hybridisation has not been performed. Hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder (9725/1, which sits outside Group II) and classic hydroa vacciniforme (not a neoplasm at all) are both unexcluded, and so is a systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disease.
alternative_entities: Severe mosquito-bite allergy (cutaneous chronic active EBV disease)
Classic hydroa vacciniforme — a photodermatosis, not a neoplasm

options.upgrade_path: EBER in-situ hybridisation with a passing control probe, plus CD3, CD4, CD8, CD56 and betaF1, would resolve 9725 (either behaviour) or exclude the family entirely.
options.coding_note: Angiodestruction is NOT required for hydroa vacciniforme-like LPD and its absence does not exclude the diagnosis. Transferability: this family is described in Asian and Latin American children; neither retained source mentions Africa for any T/NK entity, so a case coded here warrants review rather than acceptance.

options.label: Perivascular or spongiotic infiltrate without cytological atypia; or granulomatous inflammation
options.coding_note: No atypia means no lymphoma at this tier. The mimic inventory decides whether this leaves the registry.

options.label: The pattern is not determinable, or the report does not describe one
options.upgrade_path: A re-read of the section with a lineage panel (CD3, CD20, CD30, CD56) would open the entity branches.

nodes.step_label: Clinical picture of the skin lesions
nodes.question: Which clinical picture does the file describe? Read the clinic notes, not only the biopsy.
nodes.hint: This is a clinical question and in this branch it outranks the phenotype twice: a gamma-delta result never by itself moves a case with the presentation of mycosis fungoides or lymphomatoid papulosis to 9726, and a self-healing history is only decisive once ALK is negative.
nodes.coding_note: No option here emits a code. The clinical pattern chooses which marker panel opens, and it is carried forward as cutaneous_clinical_pattern into the anti-miscoding guards on g2cut_panniculitic_phenotype, g2cut_cd30_lpd and g2cut_mf_sezary. cutaneous_clinical_pattern is a variable this build coins — Pathway 5.1 has no name for the cutaneous presentation archetype (logged in G2_OPEN_ITEMS.md).

options.descriptor: Long-standing patches and plaques, often hypopigmented in a dark-skinned child, with an epidermotropic infiltrate
options.coding_note: Hypopigmented mycosis fungoides is the commonest paediatric variant and is routinely treated as eczema or pityriasis alba for years before biopsy.

options.descriptor: Erythroderma involving 80% or more of the body surface, with or without circulating atypical lymphocytes
Recurrent crops of papules or nodules that ulcerate, crust and regress on their own over weeks to months, while new lesions appear elsewhere
options.coding_note: Do not capture self_healing_history here. The behaviour criterion is asked explicitly at g2cut_cd30_lpd, and only after ALK and staging have been settled — systemic ALK-positive ALCL waxes and wanes too.

options.descriptor: A solitary or grouped nodule or tumour, often ulcerated, with no history of spontaneous regression
Papulovesicular eruption on sun-exposed skin — face, ear lobes, backs of the hands — often seasonal, healing with varioliform scars
Severe local reaction to mosquito or other insect bites — swelling, blistering, necrosis and ulceration far beyond a normal bite reaction, with fever
options.coding_note: Severe mosquito-bite allergy sits with hydroa vacciniforme-like LPD in the WHO-EORTC section cutaneous chronic active EBV disease; phenotype splits them (HV-like LPD usually CD8+ T-cell, mosquito-bite hypersensitivity more often NK-cell). It has no ICD-O code of its own — see the coding_note on g2cut_ebv_cutaneous and the entry in G2_OPEN_ITEMS.md.

options.descriptor: Deep subcutaneous nodules or plaques with a panniculitis-like appearance, with or without fever and cytopenias
Ulcerating plaques and tumours with deep dermal or subcutaneous involvement, progressing rapidly
A solitary slow-growing plaque or tumour on the face, neck or upper trunk, with a small-to-medium cell dermal infiltrate
A solitary slow-growing nodule on an acral site — ear, nose, hand or foot
Generalised or disseminated skin lesions with nodal, marrow or visceral disease
options.coding_note: Cross-tree handover. Generalised skin disease with systemic involvement is not a primary cutaneous entity; the main lymphoid tree owns it.

options.descriptor: The file establishes a non-neoplastic skin condition
The clinical picture is not described in the file
options.coding_note: Without the clinical picture the anti-miscoding guards downstream cannot fire. The phenotype node sorts on markers alone and its ceiling is 9702; record the clinical description as soon as it is obtainable and re-enter.

nodes.question: What does the immunohistochemistry report say? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: This node only chooses which entity panel opens. Where the clinical picture was recorded it is read first — a case that presents as mycosis fungoides or as lymphomatoid papulosis is sent to those panels before any phenotype rule is applied.
nodes.coding_note: Rule order is load-bearing. The clinical-pattern rules sit above the CD30, EBER and gamma-delta rules so that a gamma-delta or CD30 result can never by itself divert a classic mycosis fungoides or lymphomatoid papulosis case: those cases should be diagnosed as MF or LyP, irrespective of phenotype. EBER is a screening tick here only; the four result states are resolved at g2cut_ebv_cutaneous and g2cut_panniculitic_phenotype, which declare test_result_states.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Cross-tree. Langerhans cell histiocytosis presents in skin constantly and is not a T-cell lymphoma.
Cross-tree. Primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma (9597) and the other cutaneous B-cell lymphomas belong to the main tree.

ANTI-MISCODING GUARD. Placed above the CD30, EBER and TCR-delta rules deliberately. TCRgamma-delta expression occurs in rare cases of otherwise classic mycosis fungoides, and those cases run an indolent course and should be diagnosed as MF irrespective of phenotype.
ANTI-MISCODING GUARD, same rule for lymphomatoid papulosis. The CD30 branch still asks ALK before it asks the lesion history.
Any EBER-positive cutaneous T/NK infiltrate in a child goes to the EBV panel, where the four result states and the 9725 behaviour question are resolved.
Reached only when neither of the two clinical guards above fired. A gamma-delta population still has to be shown to be the neoplastic one before 9726 is reachable.
A cytotoxic CD8-positive cutaneous infiltrate with no clinical pattern recorded. The panniculitic panel carries betaF1 and CD56 and is the safest place for it.

nos_fallback.name: Mature T-cell lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A cutaneous T-cell infiltrate is recorded but no entity-defining marker combination was met. 9702 is the ceiling for a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with no established entity, and it is also the mandated fallback for primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, NOS — 9709 is not that fallback.

nodes.question: CD30-positive cutaneous infiltrate. Record ALK first, then the staging result, then the lesion history — in that order. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: **Rule order matters here.** Systemic ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma also waxes and wanes, so the self-healing question is only asked once ALK is negative and staging has shown no disease outside the skin. Answer ALK and staging before you answer the history.
nodes.coding_note: The flat resolution_logic list is evaluated in order and the first match wins, so the two ALK rules and the staging rules physically precede the clinical-history rule that carries the behaviour_resolution (Pathway 4.1, 3.6). Lymphomatoid papulosis types A, B, C, D and E and the DUSP22-IRF4-rearranged type are a free-text variable and never a branch — Willemze states recognising them has no therapeutic or prognostic implication. Kempf's 75% CD30 figure is the only numeric form of the PCALCL rule the corpus holds; Willemze gives no CD30 threshold, no lesion count and no regression-time cut-off, so cd30_pct is captured but never gated on.

markers: CD30 in 75% or more of the tumour cells
NPM1::ALK t(2;5) by FISH or RT-PCR

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Staging (chest X-ray, abdominal and cervical ultrasound, marrow aspirate, lumbar puncture, blood minimal disseminated disease) documents the extent; it does not change the code.
resolution_logic.coding_note: FIRST RULE BY DESIGN. This rule must precede the clinical-history rule below, because systemic ALK-positive ALCL waxes and wanes and would otherwise be captured by the lymphomatoid papulosis criterion. 9714 keeps its Layer 1 name (Anaplastic large cell lymphoma, T cell and Null cell type); under ICD-O-3.2 it is the ALK-positive code.

positive: NPM1::ALK t(2;5) by FISH or RT-PCR
resolution_logic.upgrade_path: ALK immunohistochemistry (D5F3 or ALK1) confirms the same result more cheaply and should be recorded alongside.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Second half of the ALK gate. ALK is IHC, not FISH — but where a t(2;5) result exists it carries the same consequence and must also precede the clinical-history rule.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Record the CD30-positive fraction and the clinical course. Large-cell transformation is a prognostic event on the record; it does not change the morphology code.
resolution_logic.coding_note: ANTI-MISCODING GUARD. CD30-positive large-cell transformation of long-standing mycosis fungoides is still 9700, not 9718. Placed below the two ALK rules so that an ALK-positive result still overrides it, and above the ALK-negative and history rules so that a known MF is never asked the lymphomatoid papulosis question.

provisional_pending.reason: ALK status is unknown. A CD30-positive cutaneous lesion cannot be assigned to the primary cutaneous CD30-positive family until ALK is negative — an ALK-positive result would make this secondary involvement by systemic ALCL, which is a different code and a different disease.
alternative_entities: ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma, systemic, with secondary cutaneous involvement
Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: One antibody. ALK immunohistochemistry (D5F3 or ALK1) would resolve 9714 or open the 9718 behaviour question.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Pathway 3.6: CD30-positive, ALK not done codes 9702 and the upgrade path is one antibody. Neither behaviour of 9718 may be emitted here — the /1 half would delete a possibly reportable cancer and the /3 half would assert a primary cutaneous origin ALK has not excluded.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None outstanding for the code itself. DUSP22 rearrangement (45% of ALK-negative cases) and TP63 rearrangement (2%) refine the prognosis and have no ICD-O code — record them as variables. 9715 has no Group 2 REDCap option yet, so the clerk cannot select it until the registrar adds it; the case is complete either way.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Disease outside the skin excludes a primary cutaneous entity, so the self-healing question is never reached for this case. Build contract 1: ALK-negative ALCL codes to 9714 today. Coded 9715 (ALCL, ALK negative) from 4 Sep 2026 rather than 9714.

provisional_pending.reason: ALK is negative but the patient has not been staged. Primary cutaneous ALCL requires staging showing no extracutaneous disease; without it, systemic ALK-negative ALCL with a skin deposit is not excluded, and the self-healing question cannot be applied.
alternative_entities: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma
Systemic ALK-negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma with cutaneous involvement

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Chest X-ray plus abdominal and cervical ultrasound, with a marrow aspirate, would establish or exclude extracutaneous disease and open the 9718 behaviour question.
resolution_logic.coding_note: The waxing-and-waning test may be applied only after ALK-negativity AND absence of extracutaneous disease are both established (Pathway 4.1). This rule is what enforces the second half.

behaviour_resolution.criterion: Does each individual lesion regress spontaneously within weeks to months, while new lesions appear elsewhere?

1.reason: Lymphomatoid papulosis — a chronic course of recurrent, self-healing papulonecrotic or nodular skin lesions. ICD-O-3.2 codes this /1, which places it outside ICCC-3 Group II, so the case leaves the malignant registry. Record the lymphomatoid papulosis type (A, B, C, D, E or DUSP22-IRF4-rearranged) as free text: it carries no therapeutic or prognostic implication and never changes the code.

3.reason: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma — solitary or grouped nodules that do not regress on their own, ALK-negative, with staging showing no disease outside the skin. Extracutaneous dissemination follows in only 10 to 15% of cases. A CD30-positive fraction below 75% does not exclude this: the 75% figure is one author's, and the WHO-EORTC consensus sets no threshold, no lesion count and no regression-time cut-off.

unresolved.reason: The lesion history is not recorded in the file. Coded /3 — the reportable half — pending the clinical history. Ask the clinician whether individual lesions have regressed on their own while new ones appeared. Do not default to lymphomatoid papulosis: a /1 assignment removes the case from Group II, and defaulting an unknown behaviour to /1 silently deletes a reportable cancer.

resolution_logic.coding_note: This is the clinical-history rule and it is deliberately last of the entity rules. Both preceding conditions are now established: ALK is negative and staging shows no extracutaneous disease. Lymphomatoid papulosis type C is histologically identical to primary cutaneous ALCL and the consensus concedes the distinction can be impossible on the section — which is why the criterion is a history question, not a morphological one.

nos_fallback.name: Mature T-cell lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A CD30-positive cutaneous infiltrate is recorded but ALK, staging and the lesion history were not all established. 9702 is the ceiling until they are; neither behaviour of 9718 may be assigned without them.

order: NPM1::ALK t(2;5) by FISH or RT-PCR

nodes.question: Photodistributed or bite-associated eruption with a lymphoid infiltrate. What does the EBER in-situ hybridisation show, and was the control probe read?
nodes.hint: EBV positivity is definitional here, so a negative EBER changes the answer rather than merely lowering the confidence. A negative **without a passing control probe is not a negative** — it is uninterpretable, and it has its own answer below.
nodes.coding_note: Clonality is NOT a gate: no retained source makes T-cell clonality a requirement for 9725, and a negative TCRgamma must not block the code. Angiodestruction is not required either. Severe mosquito-bite allergy has no ICD-O code of its own; this build routes it through the same 9725 behaviour_resolution because the retained sources place both entities in one section (cutaneous chronic active EBV disease) with one shared progression risk, and because the /1 half costs the registry nothing while the /3 half catches a progressor — logged for the registrar in G2_OPEN_ITEMS.md. Transferability: García-González places hydroa vacciniforme-like LPD among Asian and Latin American children and the systemic form among Asians and Hispanics; Miranda names Asians and Native Americans for the childhood EBV+ T/NK family. Neither paper mentions Africa for any T/NK entity. Expect 9724 and 9725 to be near-empty in this catchment and treat a populated one as a case for review rather than acceptance. No progression rate exists in the retained corpus and none is needed — the recode path is justified by its existence, which two sources state. Stop looking for a rate.

prior_probability.context: cutaneous chronic active EBV disease — hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder and severe mosquito-bite allergy
prior_probability.interpretation: EBV positivity is definitional in this family, so a positive EBER is expected and confirms the family rather than adding information. It is the negative result that is decisive here: a properly controlled negative EBER takes the case out of this family altogether.

provisional_pending.reason: EBER in-situ hybridisation was performed but the control probe failed, so the result is uninterpretable — it is not a negative. Nothing in the EBV-driven childhood family has been excluded, and neither has a non-neoplastic photodermatosis.
alternative_entities: Severe mosquito-bite allergy (cutaneous chronic active EBV disease)
Systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disease of childhood
Classic hydroa vacciniforme — a photodermatosis, not a neoplasm

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Repeat the EBER in-situ hybridisation on a fresh section with a probe control that passes. Record the fixation time — over-fixation is the commonest cause of a failed control.
resolution_logic.coding_note: This branch must not share a destination with the negative branch and must not emit a code the negative branch's evidence would have excluded. It therefore cannot reach 9725, and it cannot reach the non-reportable exit either.

provisional_pending.reason: EBER in-situ hybridisation has not been performed. EBV positivity is definitional for this family, so without it the case can be neither assigned to it nor released from it.
alternative_entities: Severe mosquito-bite allergy (cutaneous chronic active EBV disease)
Classic hydroa vacciniforme — a photodermatosis, not a neoplasm

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: EBER in-situ hybridisation on tissue, with a passing control probe, is the only entity-defining EBV test. Serology cannot upgrade this code and viral load has no agreed threshold, unit or specimen.

resolution_logic.reason: EBER is negative with a passing control in a papulovesicular eruption on sun-exposed skin. This is classic hydroa vacciniforme — a photodermatosis, not a neoplasm. EBV positivity is definitional for hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder, so a controlled negative excludes it. No code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

EBER is negative with a passing control in a severe insect-bite reaction. Severe mosquito-bite allergy in the WHO-EORTC sense is a form of cutaneous chronic active EBV disease and requires EBV positivity; a controlled negative makes this an ordinary hypersensitivity reaction. No code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

resolution_logic.coding_note: EBV negativity is required for both 9708 and 9726, so a controlled negative EBER is exactly what the panniculitic panel needs before betaF1 and CD56 are read.

A controlled negative EBER takes the case out of the EBV-driven family. It is returned to the general phenotype sorter rather than coded here; because EBER will not be ticked as positive there, it does not come back.

Cross-tree. EBER-positive disease that is already generalised, with fever, hepatosplenomegaly, liver failure, coagulopathy or haemophagocytosis, is systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disease of childhood (9724) or NK/T-cell lymphoma nasal-type (9719) — both owned by the main tree. This is not a skin-limited presentation and must not be coded as one.

Cross-tree. EBER-positive, CD56-positive ulcerating plaques with a cytotoxic phenotype raise NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal and nasal-type (9719), which frequently involves skin. Non-nasal presentations require exclusion of an occult nasal primary; the main tree owns that decision.

behaviour_resolution.criterion: Has the disease progressed beyond the skin — fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or a frank systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoma?

1.reason: Skin-limited hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder. ICD-O-3.2 codes this /1, which places it outside ICCC-3 Group II today. This is not a discharge: patients may have recurrent skin lesions for many years before progressing to systemic EBV-positive T- or NK-cell lymphoma, and the case must be reviewed again at every contact.

3.reason: Systemic progression — fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or a frank systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoma. The case is /3 and enters ICCC-3 Group II. Where the systemic disease is characterised, recode on review to systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disease of childhood (9724) or to NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal and nasal-type (9719): that is a recode of the same primary, not a new primary.

unresolved.reason: Whether this disease has progressed beyond the skin cannot be settled from the file. Coded /3 — the reportable half — pending review. Do not default to /1: that would remove a case from the registry on the strength of a question nobody has asked yet.

behaviour_resolution.follow_up_review: This case cannot be settled at accession and must be re-opened. Re-open it at every follow-up visit, and immediately if the child develops fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, weight loss, a rising blood EBV-DNA, or haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Progression to systemic EBV-positive T- or NK-cell lymphoma is what moves the case from /1 to /3 and therefore into ICCC-3 Group II. No retained source gives a progression rate or an interval, so no review date can be calculated — review at every contact rather than at a fixed horizon. T-cell clonality is not a gate: a negative TCRgamma does not close this case.

resolution_logic.coding_note: The 9725 behaviour is longitudinal — ICCC group membership cannot be settled at accession (Pathway 4.1, 4.6). deferrable is true and follow_up_review states what re-opens the case. Phenotype separates the two members of this section but does not change the code: hydroa vacciniforme-like LPD is usually CD8-positive T-cell, severe mosquito-bite allergy more often NK-cell.

nos_fallback.name: Mature T-cell lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: An atypical cutaneous T-cell or NK-cell infiltrate is recorded but the EBV result was not entered, so neither behaviour of 9725 can be assigned and the EBV-driven family cannot be excluded.

nodes.question: Solitary plaque or tumour with a small-to-medium pleomorphic CD4-positive dermal infiltrate. Record the phenotype, the large-cell fraction and the proliferation fraction. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: This is the only decision in this branch a pathology report can settle unaided. The question is not whether the lesion is malignant — it is whether the case is still **inside** the entity. **There is no /3 form of this code.**
nodes.coding_note: ENTITY BOUNDARY, not a behaviour split. Crossing the line does not flip /1 to /3 on the same code; it moves the case to a different code, 9702/3 (Pathway 4.1, 7.3 item 5). 9709 must never be emitted with behavior_code 3 anywhere — there is no such code, and emitting it is the single most likely invalid code this group can produce. Second trap: PD-1, BCL6 and CXCL13 are definitional for this cutaneous entity, so the rule that a peripheral T-cell lymphoma expressing two or more follicular-helper markers is reclassified as nodal TFH lymphoma (9705) must NOT fire here. That rule is nodal; a case with nodal involvement is handed to the main tree, where it belongs. proliferation_band_cutaneous is a variable this build coins to band the numeric proliferation_pct_cutaneous — logged in G2_OPEN_ITEMS.md.

markers: Large pleomorphic cells under 30% of the infiltrate

entity_boundary.reason_inside: Solitary plaque or tumour, large pleomorphic cells under 30%, low proliferative fraction, CD3+ CD4+ CD8− and positive for PD-1, BCL6 and CXCL13 — inside the primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder. Five-year disease-specific survival is 100%, staging is not recommended in typical cases, and lesions may regress after the biopsy itself. ICD-O-3.2 codes this /1, which places it outside ICCC-3 Group II.
entity_boundary.reason_outside: Generalised lesions, or more than 30% large pleomorphic T cells, or a high proliferative fraction — outside the entity. Cases like this do not belong to this category: they are peripheral T-cell lymphoma NOS and code 9702/3, which is inside Group II. This is a different code, not a different behaviour of the same one.

resolution_logic.coding_note: The entity is CD3+ CD4+ CD8−. A CD8-positive, CD4-negative infiltrate is a different problem and must not be pushed through this boundary.
A CD30-positive infiltrate belongs to the CD30 branch, where ALK is asked first.
EBER positivity takes the case out of this entity and into the EBV-driven family.

Cross-tree. Nodal or marrow involvement takes the case out of a primary cutaneous entity. The rule that two or more follicular-helper markers reclassify a peripheral T-cell lymphoma as nodal TFH lymphoma (9705) is applied there, not here — applying it to this cutaneous entity, whose defining panel is PD-1, BCL6 and CXCL13, would misroute every case.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None needed for the code. Record the Ki-67 percentage and the large-cell fraction against the case.
resolution_logic.coding_note: A high proliferative fraction is one of the three separators that put a case outside the entity, alongside generalised lesions and more than 30% large cells. Willemze gives the expected range as low, under 5% and at most 20%.

provisional_pending.reason: The proliferation fraction is not recorded. A low proliferative fraction is part of the definition of the primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder, and without it the case cannot be placed inside the entity.
alternative_entities: Primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Ki-67 on the dermal infiltrate, with an estimate of the large pleomorphic cell fraction, would settle the entity boundary.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Deliberately conservative direction. 9709 is a /1 code and sits outside Group II, so an unsupported assignment to it removes a case from the registry; 9702/3 keeps it there until the morphometry is recorded.

nos_fallback.name: Mature T-cell lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: The large-cell fraction and the lesion distribution were not both recorded, so the entity boundary could not be applied. 9702/3 is the safe side: 9709 is a /1 code outside Group II and must never be assigned by default.

nodes.question: What does the immunohistochemistry report say? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: Mycosis fungoides is diagnosed clinically and pathologically together — the phenotype supports it, it does not define it. Sezary syndrome needs the blood as well, and Sezary histology is **non-specific in as many as one biopsy in three**, so a non-diagnostic skin biopsy does not exclude it.
nodes.coding_note: Two anti-miscoding rules are encoded at the top of this list, both from the same source: TCRgamma-delta expression occurs in rare cases of otherwise classic mycosis fungoides and those cases run an indolent course and should be diagnosed as MF irrespective of phenotype; and CD30-positive large-cell transformation of mycosis fungoides is still 9700, not 9718. Clinical presentation outranks phenotype here, twice.

CD4+CD7− 40% or more of CD4 cells
CD4+CD26− 30% or more of CD4 cells
KIR3DL2+ cells 200/µL or more, or 10% or more of lymphocytes
Identical TCR clone in blood and skin

TCRgamma-delta expression occurs in rare cases of otherwise classic mycosis fungoides; those cases run an indolent course and should be diagnosed as MF or LyP, irrespective of phenotype. resolution_logic.coding_note: ANTI-MISCODING GUARD. CD30-positive large-cell transformation of long-standing mycosis fungoides is still 9700. The same rule is repeated at the top of g2cut_cd30_lpd for cases that arrive there first.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Loss of CD7 supports the diagnosis but is not required, and CD8-positive and gamma-delta variants of mycosis fungoides exist and still code 9700.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: CD4 and CD8 on the epidermotropic population, with betaF1, would raise the confidence. The clinical picture already carries the diagnosis.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Mycosis fungoides is clinicopathological. A classic long-standing patch and plaque history with an epidermotropic infiltrate codes 9700 even where the phenotype panel is incomplete.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: The clinical description of the lesions and their duration is what would resolve 9700. Mycosis fungoides cannot be diagnosed from the section alone.
resolution_logic.coding_note: A CD4-positive epidermotropic infiltrate with no clinical picture recorded. 9702 is the ceiling — and it is also the mandated fallback for primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma NOS. 9709 is not that fallback.
A CD8-positive cytotoxic cutaneous infiltrate with no mycosis fungoides picture. betaF1 and CD56 are the next question.
