nos_fallback.reason: An atypical cutaneous T-cell infiltrate is recorded but neither the mycosis fungoides clinical picture nor any Sezary blood criterion was established. 9702 is the ceiling for a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with no established entity.

order: Sezary cells over 1000/µL on the smear
CD4+CD7− 40% or more of CD4 cells
CD4+CD26− 30% or more of CD4 cells
KIR3DL2+ cells 200/µL or more, or 10% or more of lymphocytes
Identical TCR clone in blood and skin

nodes.question: Sezary syndrome is a clinical, haematological and molecular diagnosis. **A pathology report can never establish it alone.** What does the file record from the blood?
nodes.hint: Two things are needed together: an identical T-cell clone in blood and skin, **and** one of the blood criteria. Sezary-syndrome histology is non-specific in as many as one biopsy in three, so a non-diagnostic skin biopsy does not exclude it — and a benign erythroderma does not become Sezary syndrome because the biopsy was unhelpful.
nodes.coding_note: HARD GATE. 9701 is structurally reachable only through the two confirmed options below. KIR3DL2 (sensitivity 88.6%, specificity 96.3%) is what rescues the lymphopenic patient in whom the absolute-count criteria fail: of five such patients all five met the KIR3DL2 rule, while four of five failed CD7 and three of five failed CD26. Willemze corroborates the blood thresholds independently.

options.label: An identical T-cell clone is demonstrated in blood AND skin, and at least one blood criterion is met — Sezary cells over 1000/µL, or CD4/CD8 ratio 10 or more, or CD4+CD7− 40% or more, or CD4+CD26− 30% or more
options.upgrade_path: None. Both halves of the definition are met.
options.coding_note: Clone identity plus one blood criterion is the full definition. Erythroderma is the clinical half and is already recorded.

options.label: An identical T-cell clone is demonstrated in blood AND skin; the patient is lymphopenic and the absolute-count criteria fail, but KIR3DL2-positive Sezary cells are 200/µL or more, or 10% or more of lymphocytes
options.upgrade_path: None. KIR3DL2 substitutes for the absolute-count criteria in the lymphopenic patient.
options.coding_note: This is the branch that exists because the count-based criteria fail in lymphopenia. Do not send this case to 9700 for failing a threshold that cannot be met.

options.label: CD4+CD26− at or above 1000/µL is the only criterion met, and no identical clone has been demonstrated in blood and skin

provisional_pending.reason: CD26 loss alone over-calls Sezary syndrome — 8 of 154 controls met this criterion. Without a demonstrated identical T-cell clone in blood and skin the diagnosis is not established.

options.upgrade_path: TCR clonality on blood and on the skin biopsy, showing the same clone, would resolve 9701. KIR3DL2 would strengthen the blood evidence; CD26 alone will not.

options.label: Erythroderma with an epidermotropic atypical T-cell infiltrate on the skin biopsy; clone identity not established, or no blood criterion met
options.upgrade_path: TCR clonality showing an identical clone in blood and skin, plus one blood criterion (Sezary count, CD4/CD8 ratio, CD4+CD7−, CD4+CD26− or KIR3DL2), would resolve 9701.
options.coding_note: Erythrodermic mycosis fungoides. The skin disease is established; the blood half of the Sezary definition is not.

options.label: Blood flow cytometry and TCR clonality are not available at this facility; the skin biopsy shows an epidermotropic atypical CD4-positive T-cell infiltrate

provisional_pending.reason: The blood has not been examined and cannot be at this facility. Sezary syndrome is not excluded — its histology is non-specific in as many as one biopsy in three — and it cannot be assigned either.

options.upgrade_path: Blood flow cytometry with a Sezary count, CD4/CD8 ratio, CD4+CD7− and CD4+CD26−, plus TCR clonality on blood and skin, would resolve 9701. A referral for blood work is the whole upgrade.

options.label: Erythroderma; the skin biopsy is non-specific and the blood has not been examined

provisional_pending.reason: Neither half of the diagnosis is established. Sezary-syndrome histology is non-specific in as many as one biopsy in three, so the unhelpful biopsy excludes nothing — and a benign erythroderma is not excluded either.
alternative_entities: Benign erythroderma — drug reaction, atopic, psoriatic or HIV-associated

options.upgrade_path: Blood flow cytometry and TCR clonality on blood and skin, with a repeat skin biopsy, would resolve 9701 or 9700 — or establish that this is not a lymphoma at all.
options.coding_note: 9590 keeps a clinically suspected cutaneous lymphoma on the registry without asserting a T-cell lineage that neither the biopsy nor the blood has shown. Use the option below instead as soon as a benign cause is established.

options.label: The blood was examined; no clone and no criterion met, and the review establishes a benign cause for the erythroderma — drug reaction, atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, or HIV-associated erythroderma
options.reason: A benign cause for the erythroderma is established and no clonal T-cell population was found in blood or skin. This is not a reportable malignancy: no code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry. Re-enter it if the erythroderma persists and a clone is later demonstrated.

nodes.step_label: Panniculitic and deep cutaneous infiltrates — betaF1 and CD56
nodes.question: Deep dermal or subcutaneous infiltrate. Record EBER first, then betaF1 and CD56. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: **betaF1 plus CD56 is the minimum panel.** Without them a lobular panniculitic infiltrate cannot be coded beyond 9702. EBER comes first because an EBER-positive panniculitic lesion in a child is more likely to belong to the EBV-driven family than to be a panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma.
nodes.coding_note: Two anti-miscoding rules sit at the top of this list. First, the clinical guards: TCRgamma-delta expression occurs in rare cases of otherwise classic mycosis fungoides or lymphomatoid papulosis, and those cases should be diagnosed as MF or LyP irrespective of phenotype — so a case carrying either clinical pattern is sent back to its own panel before any phenotype rule runs. Second, a subset of REACTIVE T cells in subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma expresses TCR gamma/delta, so a gamma-delta population is not sufficient for 9726: the gamma-delta cells must be shown to be the neoplastic ones. Miranda confirms CD56 is not in the SPTCL phenotype at all, which makes it a clean discriminator rather than a variable one. Willemze states no histological depth criterion separating the two. gd_population_neoplastic is a variable this build coins — logged in G2_OPEN_ITEMS.md. Note that 9708 is emitted here rather than in the main tree: see the build report.

markers: Gamma-delta cells shown to be the neoplastic population

resolution_logic.coding_note: ANTI-MISCODING GUARD, first by design. A case presenting as classic mycosis fungoides is diagnosed as mycosis fungoides irrespective of phenotype, so it must leave this node before betaF1 or TCR-delta is read.
ANTI-MISCODING GUARD, same rule for lymphomatoid papulosis. Clinical presentation outranks phenotype.

Both 9708 and 9726 are EBV-negative entities. An NK-phenotype hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder mimics subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, and a panniculitic EBER-positive lesion in a child is more likely that family than 9708.

A failed EBER control is uninterpretable, not negative, and it must not share a destination with the negative branches of this node — which reach 9708, 9726 and 9702, all of which a properly controlled negative EBER is part of establishing. The case is handed to the EBV panel, which owns the repeat-on-a-fresh-section instruction and carries the provisional naming the EBV-driven childhood family. That family, with an NK phenotype, is exactly what mimics 9708 here.

provisional_pending.reason: EBER in-situ hybridisation has not been performed. An EBER-positive panniculitic lesion in a child is more likely hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder or another cutaneous chronic active EBV disease than subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, and both 9708 and 9726 require EBV negativity.
alternative_entities: Hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoproliferative disorder with an NK phenotype

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: EBER in-situ hybridisation with a passing control probe, plus betaF1, CD56, CD4, CD8 and a cytotoxic panel, would resolve 9708 or 9726.

provisional_pending.reason: betaF1 has not been done. Without betaF1 and CD56 a lobular panniculitic infiltrate cannot be coded beyond 9702, and the two entities it may be have five-year disease-specific survivals of 87% and 11%.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: betaF1 and CD56 together are the minimum panel and would resolve 9708 or 9726. Add CD4, CD8, TIA-1, granzyme B and perforin if they are not already recorded.

provisional_pending.reason: CD56 has not been done. CD56 is not part of the subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma phenotype at all, which makes it a clean discriminator against primary cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma — and without it the discrimination cannot be made.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: CD56 alongside betaF1 would resolve 9708 or 9726.

provisional_pending.reason: A gamma-delta positive population is present but has not been shown to be the neoplastic one. A subset of REACTIVE T cells in subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma expresses TCR gamma/delta, so a gamma-delta population is not by itself sufficient for 9726 — and 9726 carries an 11% five-year survival against 87% for 9708.
alternative_entities: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma with a reactive gamma-delta subset

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Double-labelling, or reading betaF1 on the atypical population specifically, would show whether the gamma-delta cells are the neoplastic ones and resolve 9708 or 9726.
resolution_logic.coding_note: ANTI-MISCODING RULE. This is the second place in this branch where a gamma-delta result must not by itself drive the code.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Germline HAVCR2 testing (mutated in 25% of cases, and up to 85% in Asian populations; its base rate in African patients is unstated) is a variable to record, not a criterion. It does not change the code.
resolution_logic.coding_note: betaF1-positive, CD56-negative, CD8-positive, cytotoxic and EBV-negative — subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma. A reactive gamma-delta subset may be present and does not change this: the neoplastic cells are the betaF1-positive ones. This code is emitted here, in the cutaneous tree, rather than in the main tree, so that the discrimination against 9726 is taken once, at one node, with both codes as available destinations.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None for the code. Record the TCR V-delta subtype (Vδ1 epitheliotropic, Vδ2 subcutaneous) as a variable.
resolution_logic.coding_note: betaF1-negative, TCR-delta-positive on the neoplastic population, CD56-positive, EBV-negative. The gamma-delta cells have been shown to be the neoplastic ones, which is what makes this reachable.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: CD56 was not positive. It is not part of the subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma phenotype, so a negative CD56 does not exclude this diagnosis, but recording it raises the confidence.
resolution_logic.coding_note: betaF1-negative with a demonstrated neoplastic gamma-delta population is the lineage definition; CD56 is supportive rather than required.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Repeat or review CD56 on the atypical population. CD56 is not part of the subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma phenotype, so betaF1-positive with CD56-positive is a discordant result and neither entity can be assigned on it.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Discordant pair. Do not resolve it by preferring one marker: send it back to the pathologist.

nos_fallback.name: Mature T-cell lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A deep cutaneous T-cell infiltrate is recorded but betaF1, CD56 and EBER were not all established. Without betaF1 and CD56 a lobular panniculitic infiltrate cannot be coded beyond 9702.

nodes.question: Solitary slow-growing nodule on an acral site with a CD8-positive infiltrate. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: **This is an indolent entity.** It looks like an aggressive CD8-positive cytotoxic lymphoma and is not one — five-year disease-specific survival is 100%, and granzyme B and perforin are negative.
nodes.coding_note: Primary cutaneous acral CD8-positive T-cell lymphoma is a provisional WHO entity with no ICD-O code. Pathway 5.2 gives the fallback as 9702 plus a site flag — never an aggressive CD8-positive code, and never 9709. Record the entity name as free text against the case so the registry does not lose it.

resolution_logic.coding_note: A CD30-positive acral nodule belongs to the CD30 branch, where ALK is asked first.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None available: this entity has no ICD-O-3 code. Record the entity name and the acral site as free text against 9702 so the case can be found again if a code is added.
resolution_logic.coding_note: The indolent behaviour trap. CD8 with TIA-1 but WITHOUT granzyme B and perforin, Ki-67 under 10%, EBV negative, solitary and acral — this is the indolent provisional entity, not the aggressive epidermotropic one.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None available for the code: neither entity has an ICD-O-3 code. Record the entity name, the lesion distribution and the cytotoxic profile as free text.

nos_fallback.name: Mature T-cell lymphoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: A cutaneous CD8-positive T-cell infiltrate is recorded but the cytotoxic panel was not completed. 9702 is the fallback for both the indolent acral entity and the aggressive epidermotropic one, neither of which has an ICD-O-3 code — record which is meant as free text.

nodes.question: Which non-neoplastic diagnosis does the file establish?
nodes.hint: Forcing an NOS malignant code here records a cancer that does not exist. Every option below leaves the malignant registry and emits **no code**.
nodes.coding_note: The exclusion inventory of Pathway 4.5, restricted to the mimics that present in skin, plus the cutaneous mimics that matter in a high-HIV, high-TB catchment. WHO-HAEM5 added tumour-like lesions to the classification precisely to prevent this error.

options.label: Cutaneous tuberculosis — lupus vulgaris or scrofuloderma — or tuberculous lymphadenitis, with a positive Ultra result and no malignant morphology
options.reason: Tuberculosis is established and no malignant morphology is present. This is not a reportable malignancy: no code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

options.label: Leprosy, or another granulomatous dermatitis with no atypical lymphoid population
options.reason: A granulomatous infection or reaction with no atypical lymphoid population is not a malignancy. No code is emitted.

options.label: HIV-associated pruritic papular eruption, or HIV-associated persistent generalised lymphadenopathy
options.reason: An HIV-associated reactive skin eruption or persistent generalised lymphadenopathy is not a malignancy. No code is emitted. Record hiv_status against the case and re-enter if an atypical clonal infiltrate is later demonstrated.

options.label: Pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis acuta (PLEVA) or pityriasis lichenoides chronica
options.reason: Pityriasis lichenoides is not a malignancy. It is the commonest mimic of lymphomatoid papulosis and of hypopigmented mycosis fungoides in children, and a clonal T-cell result does not by itself change that. No code is emitted; re-enter if the lesions become nodular, ulcerate, or a CD30-positive large-cell population appears.

options.label: Lymphomatoid drug eruption, arthropod-bite reaction, or scabies nodules
options.reason: A drug or arthropod hypersensitivity reaction is not a malignancy, however atypical the infiltrate looks. No code is emitted. Where the reaction is a severe necrotic response to mosquito bites with fever, use the EBV panel instead — that presentation is a form of cutaneous chronic active EBV disease.

options.label: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma or reactive lymphoid hyperplasia (lymphocytoma cutis)
options.reason: A cutaneous pseudolymphoma is a reactive lesion. No code is emitted.

options.label: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease, infectious mononucleosis, EBV reactivation with preserved architecture, or non-destructive post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder
options.reason: All four are non-neoplastic lymphoproliferations with preserved architecture. No code is emitted. An EBER-positive result in any of them is expected and does not upgrade the case.

options.label: Castleman disease, or IgG4-related disease
options.reason: Neither is a reportable malignancy in this registry. No code is emitted. Where HHV-8 LANA-1 is positive in multicentric Castleman disease with a large B-cell proliferation, use the main lymphoid tree instead — that is a different case.

options.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease, or juvenile xanthogranuloma and the xanthogranuloma family
options.reason: Both have no ICD-O-3 code and both take the non-reportable exit. No code is emitted. Neither is Langerhans cell histiocytosis and neither may be coded to 9751.

options.label: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), primary or secondary, with no underlying lymphoma demonstrated
options.reason: ⚠️ HLH itself has no code and takes the non-reportable exit — but in EBV-negative haemophagocytosis in a child over one to two years, **anaplastic large cell lymphoma must be excluded even without lymphadenopathy** before this exit is used. Haemophagocytosis also accompanies subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma, primary cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma and chronic active EBV disease. If any of those is established, code the lymphoma instead.

options.label: Indolent T-lymphoblastic proliferation, in-situ follicular neoplasia, or in-situ mantle cell neoplasia found incidentally
options.reason: All three are incidental low-risk lesions and must not be registered as systemic lymphoma. No code is emitted.

options.label: Progressive transformation of germinal centres, or reactive follicular hyperplasia in a node biopsied alongside the skin
options.reason: Reactive nodal architecture with no clonal population is not a malignancy. No code is emitted.

options.label: "Mastocytosis in the skin" recorded, with no marrow examination
options.reason: "Mastocytosis in the skin" without a marrow examination is a provisional clinical description, not a registrable neoplasm, and takes the non-reportable exit. No code is emitted. Re-enter the case if a marrow is later done, or if the report states a cutaneous mastocytoma.

options.label: A cutaneous mastocytoma or urticaria pigmentosa is actually diagnosed on the biopsy
options.coding_note: Cross-tree. A diagnosed mastocytoma is 9740 and is owned by the mast cell tree — this is not the same thing as "mastocytosis in the skin" recorded without a marrow.

options.label: None of these — go back to the clinical picture

nodes.question: What is in this patient's file for the histiocytic or dendritic lesion? Pick the highest tier available, or the special context that applies.
nodes.hint: This is the evidence gate. It fixes what precision is achievable and drives every 'upgrade available' line on the output block. In this subgroup the gate matters more than anywhere else in Group II.
nodes.coding_note: Entry node for tree g2_histiocytic (contract §4). Reached from the main tree's lineage node by next_node. Covers 9749, 9750, 9751, 9755, 9756, 9757, 9758, 9759. Erdheim-Chester (ICD-O-3.2 9749) is NOT built tonight — it reaches 9750 with a visible provisional (contract §1). Every path that can reach an MHN code passes through g2hist_secondary first, because prior_haematopoietic_malignancy is a required field in this subgroup, not an optional one (Goyal 2026 DX-03–05).

options.label: Referral or clinic letter only — it names a histiocytosis, but there is no biopsy report in the file
Biopsy report with H&E morphology only — no IHC performed, or none reported
Biopsy report with immunohistochemistry
Biopsy + IHC + molecular (BRAF, ALK rearrangement, clonality or NGS)
Spindled or epithelioid tumour in a node, tonsil, spleen, liver or abdomen — reported as "sarcoma" or "undifferentiated tumour", with the routine lymphoma panel non-contributory
options.coding_note: This option exists so the follicular dendritic cell branch is reachable without the clerk having thought of it first. CD21, CD23, CD35 and clusterin are not in routine panels, which makes 9758 the most likely under-ascertained code in this group (Pathway §3.8). The FDC question is put again at g2hist_panel_availability and again at g2hist_mhn_nos_review.

options.label: The file establishes a named non-neoplastic or uncoded histiocytic condition — Rosai-Dorfman disease, juvenile xanthogranuloma, HLH, indeterminate dendritic cell tumour or ALK-positive histiocytosis
options.coding_note: These are exits, not failures. Each is recorded under its own name so the registry can answer how many it saw when ICD-O-4 provides a code (Pathway §5.2).

options.label: On review this is a lymphoma, not a histiocytic or dendritic neoplasm
options.coding_note: CROSS-TREE handoff to g2_lymphoid_main's lineage node (contract §4.2 names this node g2_lineage). Roughly half of what arrives labelled "malignant histiocytosis" is something else, and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma and ALCL are both in that differential.

options.label: Malignancy excluded on review — the lesion is reactive or infective and no neoplasm is asserted
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming an entity is not the same as a panel establishing it. In this subgroup the referral is wrong about half the time, so the wording chooses which gate to run — it does not choose a code.
nodes.coding_note: This clinical_alias is unusual in emitting no malignant code. That is deliberate: at ~48% misattribution, coding a sarcoma from referral text would file roughly one wrong case for every right one. The referral-tier code (9750 with a named provisional) is emitted downstream at g2hist_panel_availability, where the missing stains can be named.

options.label: "Malignant histiocytosis", "histiocytic sarcoma", "malignant histiocytic neoplasm" or "histiocytic neoplasm" — no biopsy or IHC report
options.coding_note: No code from the wording. The four-antibody gate and the prior-malignancy field run first; the honest referral-tier terminal is 9750 with the missing stains named (Pathway §3.8.1, §9.1 item 5).

options.label: "Langerhans cell histiocytosis", "LCH" or "histiocytosis X" — no biopsy or IHC report
options.coding_note: LCH needs CD1a AND CD207/langerin. CD1a alone mistakes an indeterminate dendritic cell tumour for LCH, and a referral supplies neither.

options.label: A legacy LCH eponym — "Letterer-Siwe disease", "Hand-Schüller-Christian disease", "eosinophilic granuloma of bone" or "Hashimoto-Pritzker"
options.coding_note: These eponyms are ICD-O-3.2 Related terms on 9751/3, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, disseminated, and resolve there. 9754 is retired (registrar ruling 8, 4 Sep 2026).

options.label: "Erdheim-Chester disease" or "ECD"
"Rosai-Dorfman disease", "sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy", "juvenile xanthogranuloma", or "HLH" / "haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis"
"ALK-positive histiocytosis"
"Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma", "FDC tumour" or "fibroblastic reticular cell tumour"
options.coding_note: Routed through the mandatory prior-malignancy field, then offered the dendritic/stromal marker node. 9758 and 9759 stay in IId regardless of WHO-HAEM5 moving them to stroma-derived neoplasms of lymphoid tissues (§9.1 item 3).

options.label: The note names no entity — "histiocytic infiltrate", "histiocytosis for investigation", "awaiting biopsy"
options.reason: The note describes an infiltrate under investigation, not a malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case is not entered on the malignant registry. Re-abstract when a biopsy report establishes a neoplasm — do **not** default an unclassified histiocytic infiltrate to 9750.

nodes.question: What does the H&E description say? No IHC is available.
nodes.hint: H&E cannot assign histiocytic or dendritic lineage. Pick the dominant description; the lineage question is asked at the panel gate.
nodes.coding_note: Goyal 2026 supersedes the older "atypical mitoses with cellular atypia AND clinical evidence of rapid tumour progression" criterion. Mitotic count, atypical mitoses and Ki-67 are explicitly **not needed for diagnosis** and the consensus declines to define a number for any of them. Do not build or look for a Ki-67 threshold.

options.label: Overtly malignant cytology — epithelioid ≫ spindled; intermediate-to-large cells with abundant pink cytoplasm; pleomorphism; enlarged nuclei with round to lobulated contours; vesicular or clumped chromatin; conspicuous nucleoli; multinucleation may be present
options.coding_note: This is Goyal 2026's qualitative criterion, stated in full. It replaces the mitosis/Ki-67 rule outright.

options.label: Bland histiocytic infiltrate with no atypia — foamy or spindled histiocytes, Touton giant cells, emperipolesis, or haemophagocytosis
options.coding_note: The bland end of the family: Rosai-Dorfman, juvenile xanthogranuloma, HLH, ALK-positive histiocytosis. None of these is a malignant histiocytic neoplasm — Goyal excludes them all by name because they retain the morphology of native macrophages or dendritic cells.

options.label: Grooved or reniform (coffee-bean) nuclei with eosinophils, in a bone or skin lesion — Langerhans cell histiocytosis suspected on H&E
Spindled to epithelioid cells in a whorled or storiform pattern with admixed small lymphocytes and **no plasma cells** — a follicular dendritic cell tumour is in the differential
options.coding_note: Lymphocytes without plasma cells is the FDC morphological cue. The marker question is put at g2hist_panel_availability and answered at g2hist_fdc.

options.label: Long-bone (tibia/femur) sclerosis on plain radiographs with a histiocytic infiltrate, or perinephric / periaortic / retro-orbital infiltration — Erdheim-Chester disease is the question
options.coding_note: Plain radiographs of the tibiae and femora are an accepted ECD modality — the one ECD criterion executable without cross-sectional imaging.

captures.ecd_radiology: plain radiographs of tibiae and femora

options.label: Reviewed — reactive histiocytosis (infection, storage disorder, foreign-body reaction) with no neoplasm
options.reason: The infiltrate is reactive rather than neoplastic. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Before the panel: has this child had a previous or concurrent haematopoietic malignancy? This field is **mandatory** for every histiocytic or dendritic neoplasm — it is not optional.
nodes.hint: In children a malignant histiocytic neoplasm after acute leukaemia or lymphoma is **commoner than in adults**. Published paediatric cases are **82% male, mean age 6.6 years**, presenting **during ALL maintenance therapy** — either at about 3 months from initial diagnosis or up to 18 months after maintenance starts, not a continuous window — and **bone is the commonest site at 65%**.
nodes.coding_note: Goyal 2026 DX-03 to DX-05: document any previous or concurrent haematopoietic malignancy (including MPN/MDS) in the pathology report; test clonal relatedness when secondary MHN is suspected; report "secondary MHN" when confirmed and "MHN-AHN" when clonal relatedness is not demonstrated. More than a third of the consensus's own reviewed cases were secondary or associated. The designation changes, not the subtype code.

options.label: Yes — previous or concurrent acute leukaemia, lymphoma, MDS or MPN, and **clonal relatedness has been demonstrated**
options.coding_note: Report the designation as "secondary MHN". The subtype code is still decided by the panel and the cytology.

options.label: Yes — previous or concurrent haematopoietic malignancy, clonal relatedness **was tested and not demonstrated**
options.coding_note: Report the designation as "MHN-AHN" (with associated haematopoietic neoplasm). Not demonstrated is a result; it is not the same as not tested.

options.label: Yes — previous or concurrent haematopoietic malignancy, but clonal relatedness was **not tested**
options.coding_note: secondary_mhn_status is deliberately left unset. Recording "MHN-AHN" here would claim a clonality test that was never run — MHN-AHN means tested and not demonstrated. The outstanding test belongs on the output block instead.

options.label: No previous or concurrent haematopoietic malignancy is documented, and the question was asked
Not documented in the file — the question was not asked
options.coding_note: A mandatory field left blank. It does not change the code, but it must appear on the output block: a histiocytic tumour in a child of this age is a transdifferentiation question until someone asks it.

nodes.question: Which of the four required antibodies does the IHC report actually contain? The minimum panel is **CD163, CD1a, CD207/langerin and S100** — all four, on every suspected case.
nodes.hint: This is a gate, not a suggestion. **CD163 is the marker routine lymphoma panels omit**, and it is the first-listed required one. Answer on what was *performed*, not on what was positive — the results are ticked at the next node.
nodes.coding_note: Goyal 2026 PATH-04 requires all four on every suspected case; PATH-05 requires at least two lineage-specific markers expressed on the malignant cells, which is enforced structurally at g2hist_minimum_panel and g2hist_mhn_algorithm (every code-emitting rule there needs two positives). Langerhans cell histiocytosis is a separate matter — 9751 rests on CD1a + CD207 (Pathway §6) and is still reachable without CD163.

options.label: **All four are reported** — CD163, CD1a, CD207/langerin and S100
CD1a and CD207/langerin are reported, but **CD163 and/or S100 are missing**
options.coding_note: Langerhans cell histiocytosis is still reachable on CD1a + CD207. The malignant codes 9755, 9756 and 9757 are not — the four-antibody gate governs those, and a Langerhans cell sarcoma call additionally needs S100.

options.label: The lesion is spindled or epithelioid with admixed small lymphocytes and **no plasma cells** — follicular dendritic cell markers (CD21, CD23, CD35, clusterin) are the question
options.coding_note: Offered here as a second entry to the FDC branch. CD21/CD23/CD35 are not in routine panels, which is why 9758 is the most likely under-ascertained code in this group (Pathway §3.8).

options.label: **No IHC has been performed at all**, and the H&E describes grooved or reniform nuclei with eosinophils — Langerhans cell histiocytosis is the question
CD163 and S100 are reported, but **CD1a and/or CD207/langerin are missing**

provisional_pending.reason: The minimum panel is incomplete: **CD1a and/or CD207/langerin were not performed.** Without them Langerhans cell sarcoma and the indeterminate dendritic cell tumour cannot be separated from histiocytic sarcoma — CD1a alone is not enough, and its absence from the report is not a negative result. Coded to the provisional malignant-histiocytic-neoplasm carrier until the missing stains are done.

options.upgrade_path: CD1a and CD207/langerin on the existing block would separate 9756, the indeterminate dendritic cell tumour and 9757 from 9755. PU.1 is the tie-breaker where the phenotype stays mixed.

nodes.question: Does the H&E describe **overt malignant cytology**? This is the single criterion that separates a malignant histiocytic neoplasm from the rest of the family.
nodes.hint: Goyal 2026 supersedes the older rule. **Mitotic count, atypical mitoses and Ki-67 are not needed for the diagnosis** — the consensus declines to define a number for any of them and says they "may be of interest for future clinical-pathology correlation". Do not look for a Ki-67 threshold; there is none to find.
nodes.coding_note: Goyal's scope statement is narrower than its title: MHN covers 9755, 9756, 9757 and the uncoded high-grade indeterminate dendritic cell tumour. LCH (9751), Erdheim-Chester, Rosai-Dorfman, juvenile xanthogranuloma and ALK-positive histiocytosis are all excluded by name because they "retain the morphology of native macrophages or dendritic cells and lack overtly malignant cytologic features". 9758 and 9759 are excluded as stroma-derived. This node is where that split is taken.

options.descriptor: **Overt malignant cytology** — epithelioid ≫ spindled; intermediate-to-large cells with abundant pink cytoplasm; pleomorphism; enlarged nuclei with round to lobulated contours; vesicular or clumped chromatin; conspicuous nucleoli; multinucleation may be present
options.coding_note: Goyal 2026's qualitative criterion, quoted in full. It is the replacement for "atypical mitoses plus clinical evidence of rapid tumour progression", which is withdrawn.

options.descriptor: No overt malignant cytology — the cells retain the morphology of native Langerhans cells: grooved or reniform nuclei with eosinophils, CD1a and CD207 staining **diffuse** rather than patchy, CD68 in a Golgi dot, cyclin D1 positive
options.coding_note: Diffuse staining is the LCH pattern; patchy CD1a/CD207 with overt malignant cytology is Langerhans cell sarcoma. The distinction is taken here, on the cytology, not on the marker list.

options.descriptor: No overt malignant cytology — foamy histiocytes, Touton giant cells, fibrosis or a xanthomatous infiltrate, with long-bone, perinephric, periaortic or retro-orbital radiology
options.coding_note: Erdheim-Chester. Note that foamy histiocytes and Touton cells are **not required** under the relaxed criteria — their presence points here, their absence does not exclude it.

options.descriptor: No overt malignant cytology — very large histiocytes with round vesicular nuclei, distinct nucleoli and **emperipolesis**; S100 positive, OCT2 positive, cyclin D1 positive, CD1a negative
options.coding_note: Rosai-Dorfman disease. Emperipolesis points here but does not prove it — Goyal lists emperipolesis as non-specific.

options.descriptor: No overt malignant cytology — bland histiocytes without atypia, factor XIIIa positive, CD1a negative, CD207 negative, **after ALK-positive histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester have been excluded**
options.coding_note: Juvenile xanthogranuloma is a diagnosis of exclusion and the exclusions are named. WHO-HAEM5 drops the "disseminated" qualifier, so the same exit will arrive with differently worded reports.

options.descriptor: The report does **not state** whether the cytology is overtly malignant, and the slides are not available for review

provisional_pending.reason: **Overt malignant cytology — the one criterion Goyal 2026 requires — is not stated in the report.** Without it neither the malignant codes (9755, 9756, 9757) nor the benign-morphology entities (Langerhans cell histiocytosis, Erdheim-Chester, Rosai-Dorfman, juvenile xanthogranuloma) can be established. Coded to the provisional malignant-histiocytic-neoplasm carrier and referred for expert review. Do **not** ask for a Ki-67 or a mitotic count to settle this — the consensus states plainly that neither is needed for diagnosis.

options.upgrade_path: A slide review reporting the cytology qualitatively — cell size, cytoplasm, pleomorphism, nuclear contour, chromatin, nucleoli — resolves this. No numeric threshold is required or accepted.

options.descriptor: Reviewed — the infiltrate is reactive, and no neoplasm is established
options.reason: The infiltrate is reactive rather than neoplastic. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Overt malignant cytology is established and the minimum panel is complete. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: **S100 is what separates 9757 from 9755** — but a *positive* S100 does **not** exclude 9755, which shows patchy S100 as expected. nodes.coding_note: Goyal 2026's algorithm, applied in the consensus's own order: the CD163 branch is read first and is **CD163-positive plus one further macrophage/monocyte marker (CD68, CD4, CD14)** — it is not a triple-negative branch. The older shorthand "subtype 9750 by S100/CD1a/CD207" understated S100's role and is superseded.

The panel-completeness gate should have caught this. If langerin was genuinely not performed, the malignant Langerhans and indeterminate branches cannot be separated and MHN-NOS is the endpoint.

resolution_logic.reason: Melanocytic markers are positive. This is a melanoma — it belongs in **ICCC-3 Group XI (other malignant epithelial neoplasms and malignant melanomas)**, not Group II. Code it there; no Group II code is emitted.

S100 positive, CD1a positive, **langerin ≤5% of lesional cells** — this is the **high-grade indeterminate dendritic cell tumour** of Goyal 2026. It has **no ICD-O-3 morphology code**, and it is **never 9751 and never 9756**. No code is emitted. **Record it under its own name** in the uncoded-entity register so the registry can report it when a code appears, and refer for **expert review** — about 25% of indeterminate dendritic cell tumours behave aggressively, and Goyal's high-grade variant is the malignant end of that lineage.
resolution_logic.coding_note: ≤5% langerin is the ONLY percentage threshold the consensus adopts (PATH-06 declines to set one for any other lineage marker). Gated on the four-antibody minimum panel: PATH-04 requires CD163, CD1a, CD207/langerin and S100 on every suspected case, so this code is unreachable without all four. An incomplete panel falls through to the MHN-NOS route instead.

nodes.question: Langerhans cell histiocytosis is the question. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: LCH needs **CD1a and CD207/langerin together**. **CD1a alone is insufficient — it mistakes an indeterminate dendritic cell tumour for LCH.** The LCH staining pattern is **diffuse**; patchy staining with overt malignant cytology is Langerhans cell sarcoma, which is decided on the cytology node, not here.
nodes.coding_note: Pathway §6: CD1a+ AND CD207+ → 9751 (+ extent). CD1a+ CD207− → no code, indeterminate cell histiocytosis. The four-antibody MHN gate does not apply to LCH — 9751 is reachable on CD1a + CD207 without CD163 (Pathway §2.5, Tier 3). Langerin ≤5% is the only percentage threshold in this whole subgroup.

provisional_pending.reason: **CD1a was performed but is uninterpretable** — a failed control or an exhausted block. This is not a negative CD1a and must not be read as one. Coded **9751/3, the reportable half**, and flagged `extent_unknown`, because the alternative silently deletes a probable childhood cancer from incidence. Re-cut and repeat CD1a and CD207/langerin, then re-abstract.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: Repeat CD1a and CD207/langerin on a fresh cut with a passing control. A vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT would then settle the behaviour code.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Langerhans cell histiocytosis established on both required markers. The extent question decides the behaviour code and therefore whether the case is in Group II at all.
Langerin ≤5% of lesional cells with CD1a positive is the indeterminate dendritic cell lineage, not Langerhans. It is never 9751 and never 9756.

provisional_pending.reason: CD1a is positive but **CD207/langerin was not performed**. CD1a alone mistakes an **indeterminate dendritic cell tumour** for Langerhans cell histiocytosis — the two are separated only by langerin, and ≤5% langerin defines the indeterminate tumour. Coded **9751/3, the reportable half**, with the langerin result named as outstanding and `extent_unknown` set.
alternative_entities: Indeterminate dendritic cell tumour (no ICD-O-3 code)

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: CD207/langerin on the existing block confirms or overturns the Langerhans call. A vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT would then settle the behaviour code.

resolution_logic.coding_note: **CD1a alone is insufficient.** CD1a positive with langerin negative is the indeterminate dendritic cell tumour — never 9751, never 9756. About 25% behave aggressively, so it goes to expert review as a named uncoded entity rather than being coded to LCH for convenience.

provisional_pending.reason: Langerhans cell histiocytosis is asserted by the referral or by the H&E, but **neither CD1a nor CD207/langerin has been performed**. Coded **9751/3, the reportable half**, and flagged `extent_unknown` — the registry's default is to retain the case in Group II rather than let an unestablished single-system call delete it from incidence. The case is visibly provisional until the two antibodies are read.
alternative_entities: Langerhans cell histiocytosis, single-system (9751/1, outside Group II)

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: CD1a and CD207/langerin together establish or overturn LCH; add S100 and CD163 to complete the minimum panel if a malignant histiocytic neoplasm is also in the differential. A vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT settles the behaviour code.

The remaining differential — histiocytic sarcoma, interdigitating dendritic cell sarcoma, Erdheim-Chester, Rosai-Dorfman, juvenile xanthogranuloma, ALK-positive histiocytosis — separates first on the cytology. No Langerhans combination met and CD1a is not recorded as negative. Take the cytology fork rather than defaulting to an LCH code.

nodes.question: Langerhans cell histiocytosis is established. **Which staging imaging does the file actually contain?** The extent question is asked next, against that imaging — together they decide the behaviour code, and therefore whether the case is in Group II at all.
nodes.hint: The criterion is **≥2 organs or organ systems**, established by **vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT**. A **skull-to-mid-thigh** scan is explicitly inadequate. Record what was done, not what should have been done — the imaging modality is part of the record, not a preamble to it.
nodes.coding_note: 9751 is the highest-impact behaviour split in Group II. Config key `lch_extent_unknown_policy`, default **`retain_in_group_ii` + `extent_unknown` flag** (§9.2). Most sites have no PET-CT, so extent is indeterminate for most LCH cases; the default keeps the case in Group II because the alternative silently deletes cases from incidence. It biases toward over-inclusion, and **whichever direction is chosen must be published with the counts**. The registrar has an outstanding item to ratify or override this default (§9.3).

options.descriptor: **Vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT** performed and reported

behaviour_resolution.criterion: Are two or more organs or organ systems involved?

1.reason: Single-system Langerhans cell histiocytosis — unifocal, single-system multifocal, or single-system pulmonary — established on a vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT, the adequate modality. ICD-O-3.2 codes this **/1**, which places the case **outside ICCC-3 Group II**. Record the extent and the imaging that established it.

3.reason: Multisystem (disseminated) Langerhans cell histiocytosis — two or more organs or organ systems on a vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT. Reportable in Group II, subgroup IId.

unresolved.reason: A vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT was performed but the report does not state the number of organs or organ systems involved. Coded **9751/3 — the reportable half** — and flagged `extent_unknown`, pending a re-read of the scan. Defaulting an unknown extent to /1 would silently delete a reportable cancer from incidence, so the tool does not do it.

nodes.question: Follicular dendritic cell and stromal markers. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: **Clusterin has 100% sensitivity and 93% specificity** for a follicular dendritic cell tumour, and it is the one to ask for if only one can be afforded. The practical warning is that **CD21, CD23 and CD35 are not in routine panels** — which is why 9758 is the most likely under-ascertained code in this group.
nodes.coding_note: AUTHOR-FACING: WHO-HAEM5 reclassifies 9758 and 9759 **out** of the histiocytic/dendritic family into **stroma-derived neoplasms of lymphoid tissues** — stated independently by Miranda 2024, Tembhare 2025 and Goyal 2026 (which excludes them from MHN by name). **Both stay in ICCC-3 IId regardless** (§9.1 item 3): subgroup membership follows the ICD-O code, not the WHO chapter, and moving them would break the time series for no analytic gain. The WHO placement is recorded as a synonym note only. 9758 now covers **both** FDC sarcoma and EBV-positive inflammatory FDC sarcoma, which WHO-HAEM5 separated — record the subtype as free text against the shared code.

nodes.question: Erdheim-Chester disease is the question. What does the report show? The tool asks one marker at a time and stops as soon as the answer can no longer change.
nodes.hint: The criteria are **relaxed**. Bilateral leg osteosclerosis is **no longer required** — 5–10% of cases have no bone lesions at all. Classic foamy histiocytes and Touton cells are **not required**. S100 is **weakly positive in 20–30%**, so a weak S100 does not exclude ECD. **Plain radiographs of the tibiae and femora are an accepted modality** — the one ECD criterion executable without cross-sectional imaging.
nodes.coding_note: ICD-O-3.2 gives Erdheim-Chester disease **9749**. 9749 is built and reachable from g2hist_ecd (registrar ruling 2, 4 Sep 2026). It has no Group 2 REDCap option yet, which the output block says, and it is on docs/codes-awaiting-redcap.md. Until it lands, a confirmed ECD is coded **9750** carrying a visible provisional that names the entity — so the case stays in the registry, visibly provisional, and the switch is one line when the code arrives. `resolving_test` is recorded as Molecular/PCR because a sequencing-grade BRAF assay is the outstanding laboratory investigation; the schema's closed test vocabulary has no value for "code pending registrar action", which is the real resolving step. Written to G2_OPEN_ITEMS.md as a registrar item.

nodes.question: ALK positivity in a histiocytic lesion. **Which clone was read, and what does the lesion look like?**
nodes.hint: The clone that works for anaplastic large cell lymphoma is not the clone to read here. ALK IHC in this entity can be **very weak**, and Golgi or dot-like rather than diffuse cytoplasmic; some cases lack histiocyte markers altogether.
nodes.coding_note: ALK-positive histiocytosis is the newest uncoded entity in this group (Pathway §5.2, §9.1 item 8). Defined as a histiocytic neoplasm **lacking high-grade atypia and showing ALK positivity**. It has **no ICD-O-3 code and is never 9751 and never 9750**. Any site already stocking ALK IHC for ALCL can capture it at no additional cost — but not with the same clone. Record `alk_ihc` and `alk_clone` on every case reaching this node.

options.label: **ALK-1 or 5A4** (or another clone that is not D5F3) — positive, with at least one histiocytic marker, and the lesion shows **no high-grade atypia**
options.reason: **ALK-positive histiocytosis.** This is a named WHO-HAEM5 entity — a histiocytic neoplasm lacking high-grade atypia and showing ALK positivity, most often driven by **KIF5B::ALK** — and it has **no ICD-O-3 morphology code**. No code is emitted. It is **never 9751 and never 9750**: coding it to either would file it as a different disease. **Record it under its own name** in the uncoded-entity register so the registry can report it when a code appears. It overlaps morphologically with juvenile xanthogranuloma and Rosai-Dorfman, and diagnosis mandates IHC confirmation.

options.label: **ALK (D5F3)** — this is the only ALK result in the file
options.reason: The ALK result was read with clone **D5F3, which stains normal macrophages and is invalid in a histiocytic lesion** (Goyal 2026). This result **cannot establish ALK positivity** and must not be read as a positive. No code is emitted on this evidence. Repeat with clone **ALK-1 or 5A4**, or confirm the rearrangement molecularly — most often KIF5B::ALK — and **re-abstract**. Record the clone on the case record either way: the clone is the reason the result cannot be used.
options.coding_note: This is the not_assessable state for ALK in this subgroup. It is not a negative and it is not a positive.

captures.uncoded_entity_name: ALK-positive histiocytosis — ALK result invalid (D5F3 clone)

options.label: ALK positive by IHC, but the lesion shows **overt malignant cytology / high-grade atypia**
options.coding_note: ALK-positive histiocytosis is defined as **lacking** high-grade atypia. A high-grade ALK-positive histiocytic lesion is not that entity, so the non-reportable exit does not apply — it goes to the MHN-NOS route, which runs the myeloid exclusion and refers for expert review.

options.label: ALK positive by IHC, but a rearrangement was sought and is **confirmed absent**
options.coding_note: A positive ALK stain with a **confirmed absent rearrangement should be treated with caution** (Tembhare 2025). The entity is not established, so it does not take the named-uncoded-entity exit. Take the MHN-NOS route and refer for expert review.

options.label: ALK IHC was **very weak**, or Golgi / dot-like rather than diffuse cytoplasmic, and **no histiocyte markers are expressed**
options.coding_note: All three of these are described in ALK-positive histiocytosis — weak staining, Golgi or dot-like pattern, and cases lacking histiocyte markers altogether — so none of them excludes it. But none of them establishes it either. Molecular confirmation is the resolving step; until then the case takes the MHN-NOS route rather than a non-reportable exit.

options.label: The file names ALK-positive histiocytosis but contains **no ALK result at all**
options.coding_note: Diagnosis mandates IHC confirmation. With no ALK result the entity is asserted, not established — run the minimum-panel gate instead of taking a non-reportable exit on a referral word.

nodes.question: Which named entity does the file establish? Each of these leaves the malignant registry **with its name attached**.
nodes.hint: These are exits, not failures. Record the entity by name — without that the registry cannot answer how many cases it saw when ICD-O-4 provides a code. Forcing an NOS malignant code here would record a cancer that does not exist.
nodes.coding_note: Pathway §4.5 non-reportable inventory and §5.2 uncoded-entity map. A non-reportable terminal emits no code and has no NOS fallback (contract §4.3). Each option captures uncoded_entity_name so the case is countable later.

options.label: **Rosai-Dorfman disease** (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy) — very large histiocytes, round vesicular nuclei, distinct nucleoli, emperipolesis; S100+, OCT2+, cyclin D1+, CD1a−
options.reason: **Rosai-Dorfman disease.** WHO-HAEM5 includes it in the haematolymphoid classification for the first time, on the strength of MAPK-pathway mutations showing it is **neoplastic** — so it is a **neoplasm the ICD-O-3 vocabulary cannot express**, not a reactive condition that is not cancer. It has no morphology code, so no code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry. **Record it under its own name** in the uncoded-entity register. Note that **emperipolesis is not specific to it** — it occurs in ALK-positive histiocytosis and in malignant histiocytic neoplasms too, so emperipolesis alone does not make this diagnosis.

options.label: **Juvenile xanthogranuloma** — bland histiocytes with no atypia, factor XIIIa+, CD1a−, CD207−, **after ALK-positive histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester have been excluded**
options.reason: **Juvenile xanthogranuloma.** A diagnosis of exclusion, and the exclusions are named: **ALK-positive histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester must both be excluded first**. No ICD-O-3 code exists, so no code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry. WHO-HAEM5 **drops the "disseminated" qualifier** — the entity is now plain juvenile xanthogranuloma — so the same exit will arrive with differently worded reports. Record it under its own name.

options.label: **Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)** — primary or secondary
options.reason: **Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.** Not a reportable malignancy — no morphology code is emitted. Record it under its own name. **Haemophagocytosis itself is non-specific** and occurs in malignant histiocytic neoplasms too, so a haemophagocytic picture does not settle the diagnosis: in a child over 1–2 years with EBV-negative haemophagocytosis, **exclude anaplastic large cell lymphoma even without lymphadenopathy**, and consider systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disease of childhood.

options.label: **Indeterminate dendritic cell tumour** — S100+, CD1a+, CD207/langerin negative or ≤5% of lesional cells
options.reason: **Indeterminate dendritic cell tumour** (WHO-HAEM5's name; formerly indeterminate cell histiocytosis). It has **no ICD-O-3 code**, and it is **never 9751 and never 9756** — CD1a alone mistakes it for Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which is precisely the error this branch exists to prevent. No code is emitted. **Record it under its own name** and refer for **expert review**: about **25% behave aggressively**, and Goyal 2026's high-grade variant — the same lineage at **langerin ≤5%** — sits inside the malignant histiocytic neoplasm family even though it has no code.
options.coding_note: ≤5% langerin is the only percentage threshold the consensus adopts. Flagged to the registrar: a high-grade tumour exiting as non-reportable loses an incident cancer, and Goyal places this entity inside MHN while §5.2 gives it no fallback (G2_OPEN_ITEMS).

options.label: **ALK-positive histiocytosis**
options.coding_note: Routed to the clone node first. The exit is the same, but the clone determines whether the ALK result can be used at all — D5F3 stains normal macrophages and is invalid here.

options.label: None of these — an unclassified histiocytic infiltrate with **no malignant cytology** and no named entity
options.reason: An unclassified histiocytic infiltrate without overt malignant cytology and without a named entity. **Do not default it to 9750** — the consensus's endpoint for an ambiguous *malignant* histiocytic lesion is MHN-NOS, and this lesion is not established as malignant. No code is emitted and the case is not entered on the malignant registry. Re-abstract if a subsequent report establishes a neoplasm.

nodes.question: What reports are in this patient's file? Pick the highest tier available.
nodes.hint: This is the evidence gate. It fixes what precision is achievable and drives every 'upgrade available' line on the output block. Mast cell disease is one of the few places where the cheapest test — a smear count, or a serum tryptase — reaches a definitive code, so a low tier here is not a dead end.
nodes.coding_note: This tree owns 9740, 9741 and 9742 only (subgroup IId). Pathway confidence for mastocytosis is rated LOW and these codes are rare in children — the honest terminal here is frequently 'cannot be established from this file', which is why every node carries a route to g2mast_unresolved or to the 9740 family-level fallback rather than forcing 9741. Reached from the main tree's lineage node via next_node g2mast_document_inventory.

options.label: Referral or clinical note only — no pathology report in the file
Morphology only — skin biopsy, marrow biopsy and/or a blood or marrow smear, with no IHC, no serum tryptase and no KIT result
options.hint: A smear differential counts as morphology. It is all 9742 needs.

options.label: Morphology + IHC (tryptase, CD117, and/or CD25 / CD30 / CD2)
Morphology + IHC + basal serum tryptase and/or KIT molecular result
Reviewed — this is not a mast cell neoplasm, or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable mast cell neoplasm. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral word is not a marrow. The wording chooses the code, and at this tier the code is a placeholder with the missing test named beside it.
nodes.coding_note: Referral-only tier: confidence LOW, every downstream test listed as an upgrade. The trap this node exists to close is a note reading 'systemic mastocytosis' being coded 9741 — 9741 requires a marrow meeting the harmonized criteria (Pathway §3.8). 9740 is the family-level mast cell label and is the honest placeholder.

options.label: Note reads "mastocytoma", "skin mastocytoma" or "solitary mast cell lesion"
options.upgrade_path: A skin biopsy with tryptase or CD117 (KIT) IHC would confirm the mast cell lineage, and a stated lesion count of three or fewer would confirm mastocytoma rather than mastocytosis in the skin.
options.coding_note: 9740 is defensible on this wording because 9740 IS the mastocytoma rubric. Confidence stays low until the biopsy is in the file.

options.label: Note reads "urticaria pigmentosa", "cutaneous mastocytosis" or "mastocytosis in the skin" — no marrow mentioned
options.reason: "Mastocytosis in the skin" without a bone marrow examination is formally unclassified — it is neither cutaneous mastocytoma nor systemic mastocytosis, and it is not a reportable malignancy (Pathway §4.5). Do not code 9741.
options.upgrade_path: A bone marrow trephine and aspirate is the single step that resolves this. If it meets 1 major + 1 minor, or ≥3 minor harmonized criteria, the case becomes 9741 and is reportable; if it does not, the case stays here.

options.label: Note reads "systemic mastocytosis", "SM" or "indolent systemic mastocytosis" — no marrow report in the file
options.upgrade_path: Do not code 9741 on a referral word. A bone marrow trephine meeting 1 major + 1 minor, or ≥3 minor harmonized criteria, is what upgrades this to 9741. Basal serum tryptase is the cheapest of the minor criteria and can be ordered anywhere.
options.coding_note: The commonest error this tree exists to prevent. A clinician's 'systemic mastocytosis' is not the harmonized criteria set being met — record 9740 and name the marrow as the upgrade.

options.label: Note reads "mast cell leukaemia" or "mast cell leukemia"
options.upgrade_path: A bone marrow or peripheral blood smear with a mast cell differential count of ≥20% is what establishes 9742. That is a morphology count, achievable at any site that can read a film — no IHC, no molecular test.
options.coding_note: 9742 is a Tier 0 code (Pathway §2.6). Never emit it on a referral word; the smear count is cheap enough that there is no excuse for a placeholder to become permanent.

options.label: Note names a mast cell tumour at an extracutaneous site (bone, soft tissue, viscus)
options.upgrade_path: A biopsy of the lesion, read for overtly malignant mast cell cytology, plus a KIT D816V assay, separates mast cell sarcoma from a localised extracutaneous mastocytosis. A positive KIT D816V argues against sarcoma.

nodes.question: Which specimens does the file actually contain, and what compartment do they document? Pick the first row that applies.
nodes.hint: Read this list top down. The smear row is first because a mast cell differential count is the cheapest definitive result in this tree — if a smear with a count exists, take that row even when a trephine is also in the file.
nodes.coding_note: Compartment router. The 9742 route deliberately sits in front of every IHC gate: ≥20% mast cells on a BM or PB smear is a Tier 0 morphology count (Pathway §2.6). The skin-only row leads to the lesion-count split and, for multifocal disease, to the non-reportable "mastocytosis in the skin" terminal (Pathway §4.5).

options.descriptor: A bone marrow or peripheral blood SMEAR with a mast cell differential count
options.coding_note: Tier 0 route to 9742. No IHC gate in front of it.

options.descriptor: A bone marrow trephine and/or aspirate examined, but no mast cell percentage stated on a smear
An extracutaneous mass lesion (bone, soft tissue, viscus) reported as a mast cell tumour — no marrow examined
Skin lesions only — no bone marrow examined and no smear
Reviewed — this is not a mast cell neoplasm
options.reason: Reviewed and not a mast cell neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: How many discrete skin lesions does the file document?
nodes.hint: Three or fewer discrete lesions is cutaneous mastocytoma (9740). More than three, or diffuse involvement, is mastocytosis in the skin — and with no marrow in the file that is not a reportable malignancy. Count what the report states; do not estimate from a photograph.
nodes.coding_note: The lesion-count split of Pathway §3.8, using the §5.1 `lesion_count` vocabulary (solitary / 2–3 / grouped / multifocal / disseminated). This node is reached only on the skin-only branch, so the marrow question is already answered: there is none. That is why grouped, multifocal and disseminated terminate non-reportable here rather than continuing — 9741 is unreachable without a marrow.

options.descriptor: Solitary lesion — one discrete mastocytoma
Two or three discrete lesions
Grouped lesions in one region, total number not stated in the file
options.reason: The lesion count is what separates cutaneous mastocytoma (9740) from mastocytosis in the skin, and the file does not state it. With no bone marrow examination there is no reportable code either way, so the case exits here rather than resting on a guess.
options.upgrade_path: A stated count of three or fewer discrete lesions would make this 9740. A bone marrow meeting the harmonized criteria would make it 9741. Either is a single step.

options.descriptor: Multifocal — more than three lesions, or maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis / urticaria pigmentosa
options.reason: More than three skin lesions, or diffuse skin involvement, is not a mastocytoma — and with no bone marrow examination it cannot be systemic mastocytosis either. Each option names one specific, orderable next step. There is no 'mast cell neoplasm, NOS' code in the Layer 1 option list; 9740 is used as the family-level carrier — logged in G2_OPEN_ITEMS.

options.label: Major criterion present (multifocal dense aggregates of ≥15 mast cells) but no minor criterion documented
options.upgrade_path: Any ONE minor criterion completes the harmonized set: a basal serum tryptase ≥20 ng/mL (cheapest, and orderable anywhere), CD25 / CD30 / CD2 by IHC on the existing block, >25% atypical or spindled mast cells on review of the same slide, or an activating KIT codon-816 mutation.
options.coding_note: Marrow aggregates alone. ICC would call this systemic mastocytosis; the harmonized criteria this registry adopts do not, and the criteria_set_used capture records which framework produced the report.

options.label: The aberrant-marker panel was CD25 only — CD2 and CD30 were not tested
options.upgrade_path: Add CD30 and CD2 to the panel on the existing block. CD30 is a minor criterion in its own right, and a CD25-only panel misses well-differentiated systemic mastocytosis, in which the mast cells are characteristically CD25-negative.
options.coding_note: A legacy panel is an upgrade path, not a negative result. This is the option that stops a CD25-negative WDSM being recorded as 'criteria not met' and closed.

options.label: One or two minor criteria documented, and no major criterion (no aggregates, or no extracutaneous biopsy)
options.upgrade_path: A bone marrow trephine stained for tryptase and CD117, read for multifocal dense aggregates of ≥15 mast cells, is the major criterion. Failing that, a third minor criterion also completes the set — serum tryptase and KIT sequencing are the two most likely to be outstanding.

options.label: No extracutaneous biopsy — the mast cell disease is documented on a smear or in the skin only
options.upgrade_path: A bone marrow trephine and aspirate. Systemic mastocytosis cannot be coded without one, and a smear alone reaches 9742 only at ≥20% mast cells.
options.coding_note: Distinct from the skin-only route, which terminates non-reportable at g2mast_skin_lesion_count. This option is for a case that has some extracutaneous material but no trephine.

options.label: Bone marrow examination requested but not available at this facility — a permanent terminal state
options.upgrade_path: Record the marrow as unavailable rather than as not done, and re-enter the tool if the patient is referred to a site that can perform it. A basal serum tryptase can still be ordered locally and is worth having on the record.
options.coding_note: 'Marrow unavailable at this facility' is a legitimate permanent terminal state (Pathway §2.5) and must be recorded as such, not passed off as a completed workup.

options.label: Reviewed — this is not a mast cell neoplasm
options.reason: Reviewed and not a mast cell neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.
